issues.author: yonromai
issues.body:
## TL;DR

On H100, Transformer Engine (TE) 2.11 rejects FlashAttention 2 (FA2) version 2.8.4. An FA4 dependency override broke vLLM even with FA2 selected. RL mask guards, padding tiles, and JAX sharding had separate bugs. On GB200, batch invariance switches vLLM from FA4 to FA2. Hero's H100 FA3 window-boundary mismatch remains unresolved.

Scope: H100/GB200; vLLM, SkyRL/Megatron, and Levanter/JAX. Evidence checked on 2026-09-29. Fixed incidents below describe the cited versions; selector rules link to exact source revisions.

## Known failures

| Trigger | Observed failure | Fix or regression check |
| --- | --- | --- |
| H100: TE 2.11 + FA2 2.8.4 + context parallelism + SkyRL `trainer.flash_attn=true` | TE rejects FA; cuDNN is disabled and CP has no unfused fallback. | [#705](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/pull/705): FA2 2.8.3; real two-shard (CP2) policy forward/backward. |
| Megatron requests FA, but its runtime lacks the package | Two 64-H100 launches failed before training. | [#563](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/pull/563): import `flash_attn` and `flash_attn_2_cuda` inside the task image. |
| FA4 beta28/29 overrides FFI; the vLLM wheel was built with FFI 0.1.11 and TileLang 0.1.12 | Serving aborts with duplicate `__ffi_repr__` registration, even with FA2 selected. | [vLLM #73](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/pull/73): FFI 0.1.12/TileLang 0.1.14 were qualified together with the serving wheel. |
| Tested FA4 beta30/31 full-context Grug layers | QKV and attention-gate gradients are zero; beta31 also fails an independent output comparison. | [Historical record](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/issues/4): beta29 restored gradients; test full-causal outputs and parameter gradients. |
| RL mask `[PAD, prompt, response, PAD]` | The old guard counts two validity transitions and device-asserts on the first trainer forward. | [#255](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/pull/255): accept one contiguous interior span; test eager/FA output and gradient parity. |
| A JAX FA4 query tile starts with padding, then valid tokens | The first padded query's lower bound prunes keys needed by later valid queries. | [#7894](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/7894): carry the next valid bound backward; test causal and windowed masks. |
| A wholly padded JAX FA4 query tile skips the key loop | Pending Q copies overwrite output storage; padded outputs change on repeat. | [#8961](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/8961): drain copies; repeat the 8520-token/40-valid-token H100 case and check zero padding outputs/gradients. |
| JAX Q is batch-sharded; validity/lower-bound metadata stays global | The FA4 frontend receives incompatible local shapes. | [#6910](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/6910): shard metadata onto the same batch axes as Q. |
| Explicit JAX mesh has `data=1`; the FA4 output drops that axis | `ShardingTypeError` at the model's gating multiply during tracing. | [#9346](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9346): keep Q's complete output partition spec, including length-one axes. |

## Settings that change what runs

| Setting | Result at the linked revision | Check |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GB200 vLLM with `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` | FA4 falls back to FA2, including an explicit FA4 request. | [Selector](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/blob/39e62869693c46402b1a95fde4fc55ca1aab9ae1/vllm/v1/attention/backends/fa_utils.py#L171): log the selected version after flags. |
| General Levanter GPU attention uses the default; TE is missing | It warns and runs reference attention. Installing Grug FA4 does not select FA4 here. | [Source](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44a4188c197a4b5a314e40cc653f150fa9687dcf/lib/levanter/src/levanter/layers/attention.py#L467): explicit `attn_backend=AttentionBackend.NVTE` makes the missing import fail. |

## Unresolved numerical lead

[Hero 535B on H100](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/issues/737#issuecomment-5825046219), with FA3, eager execution, and batch invariance: cached decode and full prefill first disagree at combined target-token position 2050, just beyond its 2048-token window. The trace first changes at layer-0 attention despite equal aligned BF16 KV histories. The execution layouts differ; the kernel cause remains unknown. FA2 passed on its own generated bank, so a common-token FA2/FA3 replay is still needed.

## Open checks

- [ ] Preserve the missing Hero reports and diagnostic source in a team-readable, versioned bundle.
- [ ] Replay one common saved sequence through FA2 and FA3 to test the H100 window-boundary mismatch.
- [ ] Qualify [#9393](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9393) with H100 CP2/CP1 output, loss, and all-gradient parity; test supported GB200 layouts separately.

## Evidence and audit

<details>
<summary>Which application path applies? Backend map and terms</summary>

| Entry point | Starting point at the cited revisions | Qualification check |
| --- | --- | --- |
| vLLM serving | H100 prefers FA3; GB200 prefers FA4 when available. Batch invariance changes GB200 to FA2. Check explicit overrides too. | Inspect selection; replay the same tokens through prefill and decode. |
| TE/Megatron | Keep the qualified TE/FA pair and backend flags. | CP forward/backward, then a matched policy update. |
| General Levanter | The checked GPU default is NVTE on both accelerators. Grug FA4 installation does not change this entry point. | Force the intended backend and detect import/reference fallback. |
| Grug JAX FA4 | Check `gpu_fa4_cute` on H100 and supported `gpu_fa4_cute_sm100` layouts on GB200. | Test the adapter's masks, gradients, and sharding. Native SM100 qualification covered BF16, head dimension 128, and GQA ratios 4/6/8. |

FA means FlashAttention. TE means Transformer Engine; `NVTE` names its Levanter backend. TE has separate FlashAttention and cuDNN fused backends.

Hero is the 535B mixture-of-experts model tracked in [SkyRL #737](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/issues/737). [Grug](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/44a4188c197a4b5a314e40cc653f150fa9687dcf/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug) is Levanter's model/attention code. Scores below are target-token log probabilities; each comparison scores the same token.

CP, TP, PP, and EP mean context, tensor, pipeline, and expert parallelism. CP2 means two context shards. SM90 and SM100 name the Hopper/H100 and Blackwell/GB200 GPU architectures. GQA is grouped-query attention. Q/K/V are query/key/value tensors; Hq/Hkv count their heads; D is head dimension; S is sequence length. KV history is the cached key/value sequence. BF16 and FP32 name numeric formats. SDPA is scaled dot-product attention; ALiBi is an attention bias.

These are starting points at the linked revisions. Repeat qualification when packages, wheels, locks, or flags change.

Before changing attention:

- Record hardware, CPU architecture, Python, source/lock revisions, wheel hashes, and loaded module paths.
- Verify the selected backend after applying runtime flags. Training and serving can use different implementations in one environment.
- Test real masks, packing, sharding, and forward/backward. Include context parallelism and compare attention-parameter gradients with an independent reference.
- Compare cached decode and full prefill on the same saved tokens, weights, positions, and masks. Test across the model's window boundary.
- Measure the intended application. Keep kernel time, learner-update time, and whole reinforcement-learning step time separate.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Megatron: TE rejects the FA version, and CP has no fallback</summary>

- Incident: [SkyRL #561](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/pull/561), merged at `91e02cfc7fbd86118f96e6add4f352ef4245eb3b`, selected FA2 2.8.4 with TE 2.11 on Linux x86_64. The first old-logprob forward failed at TP1/PP2/CP2/EP8 on 64 H100s. [Echo 491](https://echo.oa.dev/wiki/491) records the rollback; [#703](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/issues/703) is closed.
- Cause: [TE 2.11's version gate](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TransformerEngine/blob/c188b533cc3721ca9c6bbfd26148f5cf60108c25/transformer_engine/pytorch/attention/dot_product_attention/backends.py#L96) accepts FA2 2.1.1–2.8.3 on H100. Its [selector](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TransformerEngine/blob/c188b533cc3721ca9c6bbfd26148f5cf60108c25/transformer_engine/pytorch/attention/dot_product_attention/utils.py#L756) disables unfused attention for CP. SkyRL's `trainer.flash_attn=true` disables TE's separate cuDNN fused backend. That combination left no backend. The rejecting component was TE's version gate.
- Fix: [Merged #705](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/pull/705) paired TE 2.11 with hash-pinned FA2 2.8.3 while keeping Torch 2.13/CUDA 13.2.
- Qualification: its [H100 policy step](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fromain%2Fmarinskyrl-fa283-cp2-nightly-bc9d5e50) passed forward/backward at TP1/PP1/CP2/EP1 with finite loss and gradient norm 8.11. The original production topology was not rerun. Direct FA/import tests in #561 had missed this application path.

Regression: verify the intended backend during a real CP2 policy forward/backward, with finite loss and attention gradients. CP1 or FSDP alone does not qualify CP2.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Native packaging: import the extension on both x86 and ARM</summary>

[SkyRL #563](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/pull/563) records two 64-H100 launches that lacked FA despite requesting it. Bootstrap now imports both `flash_attn` and `flash_attn_2_cuda` before the driver starts.

The [FA2 release](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/releases/tag/native-cu132-fa283-20260920) records FA2 2.8.3, Torch 2.13.0+cu132, CPython 3.12, and these Linux wheels:

| Architecture / qualification target | SHA256 |
| --- | --- |
| x86_64 / H100 | `4b5086728757d81c8ef89f3008b0bcea72483cf18ed96e0e31b5293ed1f01bc7` |
| aarch64 / GB200 | `9cd0731dcc8fe780aeea28480ad80456d235fc0f9cb75d92c45d2b3c233eee5e` |

Qualification covered causal/windowed/packed GQA outputs and gradients, tiny Hero updates, and checkpoint continuation on both architectures. The release makes no manylinux portability claim. [Hero #737](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/issues/737) records the separate full-model scope.

Preflight: print architecture, Python/Torch/CUDA versions, package versions, and module paths. Import the package and extension inside the actual task image, then run a representative operation. Keep wheel hashes and GPU target coverage.

</details>

<details>
<summary>FA4 dependencies: test training and serving in the same environment</summary>

[SkyRL #4](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/issues/4) records a historical FA4 beta28/29 prototype that overrode TVM FFI while keeping a vLLM wheel built with FFI 0.1.11 and TileLang 0.1.12. Serving failed with duplicate `__ffi_repr__` registration when TileLang loaded its bundled TVM. The failure also occurred with FA2 selected. SkyRL's port-collision retries hid the first native error.

[Merged vLLM #73](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/pull/73) qualified TileLang 0.1.14, TVM FFI 0.1.12, and TokenSpeed MLA 0.1.9 together on x86/H100 and ARM/GB200. The [runtime record](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/issues/4#issuecomment-5756739563) covers serving, rollout, update, and weight sync. These experimental passes do not qualify a production consumer pin.

For JAX, [open Marin #9353](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9353), head `7403f7147c71fb94c54d5dd9b28f663919ad527b`, uses FA4 beta28, CUTLASS DSL 4.6.2, and QuACK 0.6.4. Pipeline JAX is 0.11.0; Levanter's GPU extra pins 0.11.1. Earlier [H100 CP runs](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9283) used scratch JaxPP overlays. #9353's lock has not itself been GPU tested. Standalone Levanter also uses a different CPU-Torch fallback index.

Preflight: resolve the real application extra and frozen lock; exercise the adapter's kernel call; start serving from that environment. Test full-causal and local-window outputs and parameter gradients separately.

</details>

<details>
<summary>FA4 beta30/31: successful forward execution with zero attention gradients</summary>

[SkyRL #4](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/issues/4) found zero QKV/attention-gate gradients in tested full-context Grug layers with FA4 beta30/31. Beta29 restored nonzero gradients. An independent FP32 SDPA comparison also exposed beta31's full-causal output regression.

The trigger was the tested full-context path. Local-window and full-causal attention need separate checks. Compare outputs and Q/K/V plus attention-parameter gradients with an independent reference; check that expected nonzero gradients stay nonzero. A finite forward result alone misses this failure.

These are historical results for the cited experimental stacks. Later betas require their own qualification.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Backend selection: defaults, flags, and fallback</summary>

At [vLLM `39e62869`](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/blob/39e62869693c46402b1a95fde4fc55ca1aab9ae1/vllm/v1/attention/backends/fa_utils.py#L88):

| Input to the selector | Result |
| --- | --- |
| H100, FA3 available, no override/restriction | Prefer FA3. |
| GB200, FA4 available, no override/restriction | Prefer FA4. |
| `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` with FA4 selected | Fall back to FA2. This check runs after explicit version overrides. |
| Explicit FA3 on Blackwell | Use FA4 if supported, otherwise FA2; the invariance check can then select FA2. |
| ALiBi with FA3 or FA4 | Fall back to FA2. |
| Blackwell head dimension >128 | Fall back to FA2, except query/value dimensions 256/256 or 192/128. |
| Blackwell 256/256 dedicated kernel | Also needs caller support; sinks, soft capping, quantized KV, a cache block not divisible by 128, or decode context parallelism force FA2. |

Local execution of the actual selector functions checked 19 configurations with simulated hardware and extension availability. The retained Hero `d16ece36` selector has identical bytes. This checks control flow; no installed kernel ran.

Each Hero control engine used one FA version across prefill and decode. Those paths still differ in query shape, KV layout, and scheduling. Record the selector's integer version and loaded implementation; `flash_attn` package metadata alone does not identify vLLM's implementation.

At [Marin `44a4188c`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44a4188c197a4b5a314e40cc653f150fa9687dcf/lib/levanter/src/levanter/layers/attention.py#L82), general Levanter GPU attention defaults to NVTE. A missing TE import warns and falls back; explicitly requesting NVTE raises. [#7140](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/7140), the proposed general FA4 default, closed without merging. Grug's FA4 adapter uses a separate selection path.

There is another [source-visible fallback](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44a4188c197a4b5a314e40cc653f150fa9687dcf/lib/levanter/src/levanter/layers/attention.py#L162): with `use_flash=None` and `attn_backend=None`, setting a `flash_block_size` that does not divide the query or key length selects vanilla attention. This rule was read from source; it was not part of the local import-fallback checks.

Preflight: inspect the running worker after all flags are set. For JAX, force the backend and inspect lowering or a profile to catch reference fallback.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Masks and padding: three distinct failures</summary>

| Failure | Cause and fix | Tested scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| RL mask guard rejected valid batches | Left-padded prompts and right-padded responses create one interior valid span. [SkyRL #254](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/issues/254) led to [merged #255](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/pull/255), which accepts that span and rejects empty/discontiguous rows. | Eager/FA outputs and gradients on an RL-shaped H100 batch. |
| Leading padding removed needed key tiles | The first-query lower-bound sentinel could prune keys needed later in the tile. [Merged Marin #7894](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/7894) repaired it. | D128 H100 causal/windowed outputs and gradients against FP32 attention. |
| Wholly padded outputs changed on repeat | Pending asynchronous Q copies overwrote output storage when an empty key loop skipped its wait. [Merged #8961](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/8961) fixed the race; [Echo 358](https://echo.oa.dev/wiki/358) records before/after results. | H100: S8520, Hq20, Hkv5, D128, BF16, 40 valid prefix tokens, and a wholly padded row. An S384 probe missed it. |

Minimal mask illustrating the first failure: validity `[0, 0, 1, 1, 1, 0]` has two transitions but one valid span. The old `transitions <= 1` guard rejects it. The adopted fix counts valid-span starts and still rejects empty/discontiguous rows.

The leading-padding fix had before/after H100 evidence: 62.0% of full-causal and 67.5% of sliding-window valid outputs mismatched the FP32 reference before the fix; the metadata and both output/gradient cases passed afterward. The wholly padded tile race was a separate failure in asynchronous copy handling.

Regression: cross a tile with interior spans and packed boundaries. Check causal/windowed masks, zero padding outputs/gradients, and exact repeats. For the S8520 case, use a dense reference over the valid 40-token prefix to avoid an 8520² allocation.

</details>

<details>
<summary>JAX and context parallelism: metadata, offsets, and compiler control</summary>

- [Merged #6910](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/6910) reshards FA4 lower-bound/validity metadata onto batch axes before `shard_map`. Its regression checks matching local metadata and Q shapes.
- [Merged #9346](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9346) keeps length-one mesh axes in the output partition spec. Dropping `data=1` broke tracing at the model's gating multiply. The regression substitutes a kernel; it does not test CUDA numerics.
- [Native SM100 #9332](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9332) qualifies BF16/D128 GQA ratios 4/6/8. Context-sharded Q needs global offsets, full K/V on each shard, and summed partial K/V gradients.
- [Open #9393](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9393), head `529715fc3951ca0c74d3083cb56a1e4d0ead66c1`, changes native SM90 backward offsets/frontend dispatch and rejects unsupported native SM100 layouts. GPU qualification is pending.
- [Open #7529](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7529) records a JaxPP-localized BF16 backward compiler exit 139. The same two-host EP8 computation passed with `distributed_direct`.

Next check: compare H100 CP2 with CP1 outputs, loss, and all gradients using nonzero global query offsets, packed boundaries, and local windows. Run GB200 supported-layout checks separately. Keep the execution-mode control for compiler failures.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hero H100: FA3 log probabilities differ beyond the 2048-token window</summary>

The [Hero numerical record](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/issues/737#issuecomment-5825046219) locates the first tensor split at layer-0 FA3 attention beyond Hero's 2048-token window.

Both controls used step-108000 BF16 weights, 32 pinned GSM8K prompts, H100, batch invariance, eager execution, no KV padding, and a 4096-token combined cap. Counts below total the 32 responses in each bank. vLLM source was `d16ece36c45f67fdbbdd9968a3a71e4d9fb97b79`.

| Control | Response tokens | Decode versus same-response full-prefill log probabilities |
| --- | --- | --- |
| FA3, source `37d0e6b2`, job `/hero-vllm/hero-vllm-qualification-e3f98f6650b7` | 9472 | 2044 differed, all on one capped response, capture ID `rank-17`. First difference: reported combined position 2050 (169 prompt tokens + response index 1881). |
| FA2, source `458b104b`, job `/hero-vllm/hero-vllm-qualification-e80c432e8dce` | 12241 | Exact on its own generated bank. |

The qualification sources differed only in FA version and report field. The generated token banks differed, so these controls do not compare FA2 and FA3 on identical tokens.

Trace `/hero-vllm/hero-vllm-qualification-e79d53666638`, source `3fa62e87`, replayed the saved FA3 response:

- At reported input position 2049, current-token projections and aligned BF16 KV histories were exact. The first target-log-probability difference was at the next combined token position, 2050.
- The full-prefill capture also had nine extra rows marked position zero. This audit did not verify their mask treatment; exact aligned histories do not establish identical execution layouts.
- Layer-0 raw attention first changed in 75/6144 BF16 coordinates, with max gap 0.00048828125. A later layer-5 expert choice changed.

The trace identifies the tested attention path. The kernel instruction cause remains unknown.

Recorded report/tensor roots:

```text
s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/users/romain/hero-grouped-rl-01a0bca4/h100-fa3-window-control-37d0e6b2/
s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/users/romain/hero-grouped-rl-01a0bca4/h100-fa2-window-control-458b104b/
s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/users/romain/hero-grouped-rl-01a0bca4/h100-fa3-window-trace-3fa62e87/
```

An earlier GB200 FA2 split at position 2045 had not equated all cached KV history. Changing only experimental embedding-down arithmetic from FP32 to BF16 removed that split, while an independent H100 dot-product reference favored FP32 on its tested input. This gives no universal precision fix. Ablation source: `9a325f5051d627cf56b5e3ecabf229ff8435398f`; recorded results:

```text
s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/users/romain/hero-numerical-resolution/vllm-prefill-decode-attn-probe-original-bf16-embed-down-9a325f5051
```

[Snowball #7554](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7554) separately traced short-prompt rank divergence to expert-parallel reduce-scatter and routing amplification. Its unresolved long-prompt effects do not establish the Hero FA boundary failure.

Next check: replay one saved sequence through FA2 and FA3 across the window/block boundary. Hold tokens, positions, weights, masks, and KV history fixed. Trace the first attention difference, expert routes, and same-token log probabilities; compare saved Q/K/V with an independent reference.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Performance: measured application results and their limits</summary>

The September 29 Hero learner comparison held the checkpoint, token bank, topology, precision, and shared NCCL settings fixed. Source: `a9d7e75dff870e6ed02c217ffa4070b74e34cb73`; step-144000 BF16 model; 128 sequences/116351 unpadded tokens; TP1/PP12/EP4/CP4 on 48 GB200s; MuonH/AdamH/Adam optimizers; no profiler. The configuration changed `trainer.flash_attn` and run identity.

| Measurement | Requested TE fused mode | Requested flash mode |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Median later warm update | 63.303 s | 61.180 s |
| Median captured-route score replay, 51326 tokens | 20.254 s | 19.975 s |
| Probability-ratio outliers outside [0.8, 1.2] | 5 | 4 |
| Replay gate | Passed | Passed |

The [fixed-weight gate](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/issues/737) allows fewer than 0.1% of same-token trainer/serving probability ratios outside [0.8, 1.2]. Every replay trial scored 51326 tokens: each of the four fused-mode trials had five outliers, and each of the four flash-mode trials had four. Scores are target-token log probabilities; ratios compare their exponentiated values. This replay bank is separate from the 116351-token update bank.

Reports record requested modes but lack a selected TE kernel trace. There was one placement per arm. The result does not establish an online RL gain or H100 speed ranking.

Reports and hashes:

```text
Fused: s3://hero-checkpoints/marin/users/romain/hero-perf-01a0e406/gb200-tim-fused-48g-a2/report.json
SHA256: fc76835736d86baacbcc1f8bfc0d38c973eb4bc72db0dbb2b5e362bbecfeca51
Flash: s3://hero-checkpoints/marin/users/romain/hero-perf-01a0e406/gb200-tim-flash-48g-a1/report.json
SHA256: a482ca6521a353cd511dd99cce4721850f52d6c5204041dcf48a95c9b3a64405
```

Iris jobs were `/romain/hero-gb200-tim-fused-48g-01a0e406-a2` and `/romain/hero-gb200-tim-flash-48g-01a0e406-a1`. The audit verified retained report hashes and recomputed medians from three later warm updates and four score-replay trials. Live S3 retrieval and publication of source `a9d7e75d` remain gaps.

For JAX/GB200, [#9332](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9332) reports three matched 64-GPU pairs: native SM100 backward improved training throughput 4.03%. The [exact backward results](https://github.com/mcwitt-agent/marin/blob/9cf80aafb65b1b146e9655b3f9d4346e96252ed8/experiments/benchmarks/sm100_rebased_results.json) give median update times 15.805194/15.192662 s. Four pairs were planned; the study stopped after three following interim results. Its intervals are descriptive.

A separate native-forward study measured 4.02% with native backward in both arms. No single paired run measures the combined gain. Tile 128×64 improved short packed-document forward time from 2.74 to 2.10 ms but worsened long full-causal time from 3.25 to 3.58 ms; the default stayed 128×128.

[SkyRL's trained FA2/FA4 comparison](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/issues/4#issuecomment-5756739563) found a small attention/scoring gain without a resolved whole-step benefit. Repeated prompts became prefix-cache dominated and all learning signals were zero.

Its [unchanged-checkpoint route replay](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/issues/4#issuecomment-5788607838) passed the fixed finite/max<0.2/mean<0.03 score-gap gate with both backends: FA2 max/mean 0.04700565/0.01122633; FA4 0.05504990/0.01125093. Exact probe/output archives are embedded in that comment. The first natural-route divergence remains unexplained.

Benchmark: pass correctness gates first. Fix weights, tokens, precision, topology, flags, and denominator; warm compilation; pair placement/order where possible. Report application time alongside kernel time.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Audit scope, evidence access, and link lifetime</summary>

The audit read live GitHub records, exact source revisions/locks, original run reports, and both Echo incidents. Local checks executed actual selector/fallback functions with simulated hardware/import availability, exported the frozen Megatron dependency selection, verified published replay archives, and recomputed retained performance results. No new GPU jobs ran.

The detailed Hero reports `HERO-H100-FA3-WINDOW-CONTROL-20260924.md` and `MEGATRON-HANDOFF.md` were read from retained session artifacts. Six Hero source commits did not resolve through the checked team/personal GitHub repositories. S3 reads failed because storage credentials were absent; object availability remains unverified. Historical Iris outcomes came from retained reports.

| Reference | Preservation limit |
| --- | --- |
| Full-commit GitHub code links | Fix the code version; availability still depends on repository/commit preservation. |
| Issues, PRs, and comments | Generally long lasting; text can be edited or deleted. |
| Native FA2 release | API reports `immutable: false`. Hashes verify bytes but do not preserve them. |
| Echo | Team access required. Notes are intended to persist; no retention/migration guarantee was verified. |
| Iris | Team access required. [Current source](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/e49f36f2d7434776d9289a6bf3781f22b419ba39/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/controller.py#L283) defaults to deleting terminal jobs after seven days. The deployed setting for these jobs was not verified. |
| Recorded S3 paths | Outside explicit TTL scratch prefixes; bucket retention and current availability were not verified. |

To read an authenticated S3 report: `uv run fsutil cat <report-uri> --raw`.

Before an upstream bug report, preserve the essential Hero reports and exact diagnostic source in a team-readable, versioned bundle, and verify the recorded objects. This issue preserves the measured summary and marks the remaining access gaps.

issues.body: ## TL;DR SFT on MiniSweAgent-format traces raises Grug-67B-A2B 09.21 from 0.118 to 0.255 pass@1 on OT-TB-Lite (68 tasks, 3 seeds). The paired difference is +0.137, 95 % CI [+0.083, +0.196]. The same checkpoint scores 0.120 against 0.091 on Terminal-Bench 2.0 (+0.027 [-0.023, +0.076]) and 0.090 against 0.083 on Terminal-Bench 2.1 (+0.006 [-0.026, +0.041]). Neither Terminal-Bench interval excludes zero. Adding the base model's own passing rollouts to the teacher traces moves OT-TB-Lite from 0.211 to 0.245 at 18% of training tokens and to 0.255 at 31%. Both steps are inside the noise of three seeds (run 7 - run 6: +0.034 [-0.034, +0.103]; run 10 - run 7: +0.010 [-0.049, +0.069]). ## Description Base model: `open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.09.21`. We fine-tune it on agent traces and evaluate each checkpoint on three terminal-agent benchmarks: - OT-TB-Lite: `DCAgent/dev_set_v2`, 100 tasks, of which 68 are scored here (see Caveats). - Terminal-Bench 2.0: 89 tasks, 88 scored by every checkpoint. - Terminal-Bench 2.1: `harbor-framework/terminal-bench-2-1` at `7131e43`, 89 tasks. Terms used below: - MiniSweAgent (MSA): a harbor agent in mini-swe-agent's style. Native OpenAI tool calls, one `bash` tool with a persistent shell, reasoning from every earlier turn kept in the history, no compaction. The run ends after three consecutive turns without a tool call. - Teacher traces: the success split of `allenai/tmax-sft` (teacher Qwen 3.6 27B), subset `skill_tax_20260505_2.2k_combined_balanced_thinking_only_success`. 5,795 rows in, 5,324 training rows (37.0M tokens, 1,060 tasks) after dropping rows with function-call fragments in the text, tool calls other than `bash`, and rows longer than 32,768 tokens. - RFT (rejection fine-tuning): training on the model's own rollouts that passed the grader. The rollouts are 8 attempts per task by the base model under MiniSweAgent on 400 Endless Terminals tasks (`obiwan96/endless-terminals`) and 374 Recursive-Task-Synthesis tasks (`Zhongzhi1228/Recursive-Task-Synthesis`): 6,184 trials. A trial is kept if its reward is 1.0, its last turn submits, and no command reads a test, solution or grader path. 2,146 trials pass these filters, from 550 tasks. ## Results The charts and the tables below show the same numbers. Pass means reward == 1.0. Three seeds per row. Brackets are Wilson 95 % intervals on pooled trials. ``` OT-TB-Lite, 68 tasks passes/trials pass@1 95 % interval per seed base, Terminus-2 29/203 0.143 [0.101, 0.198] 6/68 12/67 11/68 base, MiniSweAgent 24/204 0.118 [0.080, 0.169] 10/68 8/68 6/68 run 5r Terminus-format mix, 15 % RFT 28/204 0.137 [0.097, 0.191] 13/68 5/68 10/68 run 6 teacher traces only 43/204 0.211 [0.160, 0.272] 15/68 14/68 14/68 run 7 teacher traces + 18 % RFT 50/204 0.245 [0.191, 0.308] 16/68 14/68 20/68 run 10 teacher traces + 31 % RFT 52/204 0.255 [0.200, 0.319] 18/68 19/68 15/68 Terminal-Bench 2.0, 88 tasks base, Terminus-2 12/259 0.046 [0.027, 0.079] 7/85 3/88 2/86 base, MiniSweAgent 24/263 0.091 [0.062, 0.132] 6/87 10/88 8/88 run 5r 22/262 0.084 [0.056, 0.124] 8/86 6/88 8/88 run 6 26/264 0.098 [0.068, 0.140] 9/88 8/88 9/88 run 7 30/262 0.115 [0.081, 0.159] 8/86 9/88 13/88 run 10 31/259 0.120 [0.086, 0.165] 11/85 11/88 9/86 Terminal-Bench 2.1, 89 tasks base, MiniSweAgent 22/265 0.083 [0.055, 0.122] 6/89 7/88 9/88 run 5r 16/262 0.061 [0.038, 0.097] 6/87 4/87 6/88 run 7 24/260 0.092 [0.063, 0.134] 7/87 8/86 9/87 run 10 24/266 0.090 [0.061, 0.131] 8/88 7/89 9/89 ``` Paired differences in per-task pass rate, bootstrap over tasks, 20,000 resamples. "up/down" counts tasks whose pass rate rose or fell. ``` OT-TB-Lite Terminal-Bench 2.0 Terminal-Bench 2.1 run 5r - base MSA +0.020 [-0.020, +0.059] 10/5 -0.008 [-0.042, +0.027] 7/9 -0.024 [-0.067, +0.017] 4/10 run 6 - base MSA +0.093 [+0.034, +0.152] 18/4 +0.008 [-0.034, +0.053] 10/10 not run run 7 - base MSA +0.127 [+0.078, +0.181] 20/0 +0.023 [-0.030, +0.080] 10/9 +0.006 [-0.034, +0.047] 8/8 run 10 - base MSA +0.137 [+0.083, +0.196] 23/2 +0.027 [-0.023, +0.076] 10/7 +0.006 [-0.026, +0.041] 7/8 run 7 - run 6 +0.034 [-0.034, +0.103] 18/12 +0.015 [-0.027, +0.057] 10/7 not run run 10 - run 7 +0.010 [-0.049, +0.069] 15/14 +0.004 [-0.038, +0.045] 10/8 +0.000 [-0.030, +0.030] 8/8 base MSA - base T2 -0.025 [-0.074, +0.025] 5/10 +0.045 [+0.008, +0.087] 13/5 not run ``` What the numbers support: - Runs 6, 7 and 10 beat the base on OT-TB-Lite. No task got worse under run 7. - No checkpoint is separable from the base on Terminal-Bench 2.0 or 2.1 at three seeds. - RFT is directionally positive on OT-TB-Lite and Terminal-Bench 2.0. Going from 18 % to 31 % changes nothing we can measure. - On the base model, MiniSweAgent scores twice Terminus-2 on Terminal-Bench 2.0 and is indistinguishable from it on OT-TB-Lite. Terminus-2 rejects 68-81 % of the base model's turns as unparseable JSON; MiniSweAgent rejects about 5 %. - Run 5r was trained on Terminus-2-format data and is evaluated here under MiniSweAgent, a format it never saw in training. It is not a test of RFT under MiniSweAgent. ## Training data per run ``` run mix rows tokens composition 5r mix_64k_v5r 43,129 740.3M AgentTrove 18,624; Recursive-Task-Synthesis teacher rollouts 7,641 and failure prefixes 4,417; Bespoke 903; 1,443 RFT rows from an earlier SFT checkpoint's rollouts, each repeated 8 times (14.6 % of tokens). Terminus-2 JSON actions. 6 tmax_msa_v1 5,324 37.0M teacher traces only 7 mix_v7 6,301 45.0M teacher traces + 977 RFT rows (622 Endless Terminals, 355 Recursive-Task- Synthesis), at most 2 per task, 8.05M tokens = 17.9 % 10 mix_v9 7,363 53.6M teacher traces + 2,039 RFT rows (1,501 + 538), at most 8 per task, 16.65M tokens = 31.1 % ``` Within the per-task cap, RFT rows are chosen by fewest turns. Assistant turns without a tool call are removed from RFT rows together with the harness's format-error reply. Rows are stored as OpenAI-style messages with the `bash` tool schema and rendered by the base model's own chat template, so training text matches what vLLM sends at serving. ## Training settings Levanter, 16 nodes of 4 GH200 GPUs. Weights-only initialisation from the base export with a fresh optimizer. ``` optimizer AdamH, learning rate 1e-4, beta1 0.9, beta2 0.95, epsilon 1e-8, weight decay 0, grad clip 1.0 schedule cosine, 3 % warmup, floor 0.1 of peak batch 64 packed sequences per step loss assistant tokens only router biases frozen at the imported values, router weights trained run 5r sequence length 65,536, 2 epochs, 354 steps runs 6, 7, 10 sequence length 32,768, 3 epochs, 54 / 66 / 78 steps export bf16 safetensors, max_position_embeddings set back to 262,144 ``` Runs 6, 7 and 10 train and export with the base model's chat template. Run 5r trained with a template that omits the `Reasoning: /think` system header. ## Evaluation settings ``` harbor 0.22.0, Daytona sandboxes (daytona 0.211.2), litellm 1.100.0, auto_snapshot on agent MiniSweAgent, temperature 1.0, max_tokens 16,384, no step cap, stop after 3 consecutive format errors, reasoning kept in history timeouts timeout_multiplier 3.0 on every suite concurrency 16 trials per job seeds 3 per checkpoint, one vLLM server per seed vLLM Marin fork (0.0.0.dev20260804+marin.fa50698a9a30), one node of 4 GH200 GPUs, bf16, data-parallel 4 with expert parallel, 1 API server, max-model-len 262144, max-num-seqs 32, max-num-batched-tokens 16384, prefix caching, chunked prefill, FlashInfer attention, Grug reasoning parser, hermes tool-call parser with auto tool choice ``` Scoring rules, applied identically to every row: - A trial without a verifier reward (sandbox or server error) is excluded, not counted as a failure. - Trials are deduplicated by task and seed. When a job and its rerun of unfinished trials both scored a cell, the first job's value stands. - Each suite is restricted to the tasks that every checkpoint scored at least once. ## Caveats - OT-TB-Lite covers 68 of 100 tasks. The other 32 need their own Daytona snapshots and the org is at its 40-snapshot cap. The 68 are the same set for every checkpoint. - All runs use 3x the default task timeouts, to separate capability from verbosity. Runs at 1x are not done yet. - Three seeds cannot resolve differences below about 3 points on these suites. - Terminal-Bench 2.1 numbers should not be compared with 2.0 numbers. 25 of the 89 tasks changed what the agent sees, and the 2.1 evals ran as one batch of 12 concurrent jobs, where the 90th-percentile environment setup time was 66.8 s against 9.6 s for 2.0. Within 2.1 all four checkpoints ran under the same conditions. - The base model under Terminus-2 was served without the reasoning parser. Part of its rejected turns may come from that. - Most of run 5r's trials were sent an earlier wording of the `bash` tool description. Base and runs 6, 7 and 10 were all sent the current wording. - Partial credit exists only on OT-TB-Lite and is not counted as a pass. ## Status - Done: OT-TB-Lite and Terminal-Bench 2.0 for base (both harnesses), runs 5r, 6, 7, 10. Terminal-Bench 2.1 for base, runs 5r, 7, 10. - Not done: run 6 on Terminal-Bench 2.1, and every checkpoint at 1x timeouts. - Running: RL from the run 7 checkpoint on the tasks where run 7 passes some but not all of 8 attempts. ## Links - Code: the trainer branch, the MiniSweAgent harbor agent and the vLLM parser plugins are being cleaned up and will be linked in a comment. ## Decision Log - MiniSweAgent is the harness for evaluation, SFT data and RL rollouts. Terminus-2 rejects most of this model's turns, and SFT on Terminus-format data (runs 1-5r) raised the accepted share without raising Terminal-Bench 2.0 pass rate. - Train with the base model's chat template from run 6 on. Earlier runs used a template without the reasoning header. - Freeze router biases. An unfrozen run overwrote the imported biases at step 0. - One vLLM server per seed. Seed jobs that share a server are correlated through a sticky connection to one API-server process. - Stop tuning the RFT share. Runs 7 and 10 differ by less than the seed noise on all three suites. ## Conclusion SFT on teacher traces in the MiniSweAgent format gives a measurable gain on OT-TB-Lite and none we can measure on Terminal-Bench 2.0 or 2.1. RFT from the base model's own passes adds at most a few points and saturates by 18 % of tokens. Verified traces from other sources and RL are the next things to test.

issues.author: dlwh
issues.body:
Root `pyproject.toml` or `uv.lock` edits select the full Levanter TPU suite even when the changed dependencies are unrelated to that runtime. This spends TPU CI time on verifier-only dependency changes and can exceed the job's 25-minute limit.

In #9567, extracting the verifier into `marin-community/verifyit` changed its workspace dependency to a pinned Git dependency. The lock diff did not change JAX, jaxlib, libtpu, or other transitive package versions, and the PR changed no Levanter or Haliax source. [CI run 36634897489](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/36634897489) reported `reason: broad-trigger`. The [TPU retry](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/36634897489/job/109646333278) selected 1,823 cases and printed `1566 passed, 258 skipped, 173 deselected` before the job timed out with exit code 124. The skipped total includes one collection skip, outside the 1,823 selected cases. There were no test assertion failures in that summary.

Reproduce:

1. In a checkout of #9567 at `fad8e9d6ebbe1ffcc6d3d3b9cb8820ec5d5da791`, run `uv run --no-project infra/ci/select_tests.py --base-ref d929102c0afc0282cda588d57001b2be8a9a62ad`. This only computes selection.
2. Observe `broad-trigger` and the broad `levanter-tpu` path list despite the verifier-only dependency change.

Expected: this extraction retains CPU verifier and Marin integration coverage without requiring TPU tests.

The [selector](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/fad8e9d6ebbe1ffcc6d3d3b9cb8820ec5d5da791/infra/ci/select_tests.py#L70-L78) treats both root manifests as broad triggers. They also [trigger the accelerator lanes](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/fad8e9d6ebbe1ffcc6d3d3b9cb8820ec5d5da791/infra/ci/select_tests.py#L159-L166); the resulting full Levanter selection sends non-Torch tests to TPU, including tests that also run on CPU.

Proposed fix:

- Keep existing broad CPU coverage for root manifest edits. Gate the TPU lane on semantic changes to the resolved dependencies used by its CI command: `marin-levanter`, its `tpu` extra, and its test dependencies, including their transitive dependencies. Compare base and head versions, sources, markers, extras, and dependency edges. Comparing the entire workspace graph or only a package-name allowlist would not distinguish unrelated changes safely.
- Preserve current selection for Levanter/Haliax source and CI selector/workflow changes, explicit full-suite runs, and changes whose dependency impact cannot be determined safely.
- Add selector regressions for this extraction selecting no TPU lane, TPU runtime or shared transitive dependency changes selecting the lane, and unavailable or unparseable dependency graphs falling back to broad selection. Preserve scheduled full-suite coverage.

2. Compare normalized reachable package identities (name, version, source, selected markers and artifacts) and dependency edges, including requested extras. A changed shared transitive dependency or edge selects TPU; a change confined to the verifier or another unrelated workspace package does not. If either lockfile is missing, malformed, uses an unsupported shape, has ambiguous edges, or root manifest settings may affect this install outside the compared graph, select TPU conservatively.

Current code gives selector/workflow edits broad CPU coverage but no TPU suite (`test_selector_changes_do_not_wake_the_accelerator_suites` asserts this). `--run-all-tests` with a base ref also gates extra suites by diff; only the no-base invocation selects every suite. issues.body:
<!-- experiment-tldr:start -->
## Summary

This issue records evidence-labeled hardware inputs for Marin training cost models. The current usable facts are H100 per-GPU compute/HBM measurements, Blackwell-proxy compute/HBM measurements kept separate from GB200/NVL72 claims, H100 two-node all-reduce through 1 GiB, and partial H100 reduce-scatter through 256 MB. The conclusion is intentionally conservative: H100 compute, HBM, and all-reduce are backed well enough for current planner inputs; reduce-scatter is only partially backed; native NCCL all-gather/reduce-scatter plus local GB200/NVL72 measurements remain open before those rows should be treated as firm objective inputs.

### Helpful links
- Report: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/codex/gpu-hardware-target-report/.agents/reports/gpu-hardware-target-report.md
- Logbook: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/codex/gpu-hardware-target-report/.agents/logbooks/gpu-hardware-target-assumptions.md
- Benchmark harness: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/codex/gpu-hardware-target-report/scripts/bench/gpu_microbench.py
- Snapshot commit: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/commit/b306b74b25
<!-- experiment-tldr:end -->

## TL;DR

We have measured H100 and Blackwell-proxy compute/HBM inputs and a partial collective bandwidth matrix for training cost modeling. H100 per-GPU bf16/fp8/HBM inputs are experimentally grounded in our JAX stack. H100 two-node all-reduce is measured through 1 GiB, and H100 two-node reduce-scatter is measured through 256 MB. GB200/NVL72 values are source-backed or inferred, not locally measured. Native NCCL all-gather/reduce-scatter and GB200/NVL72 measurements remain open.

## Description

This issue tracks the hardware evidence used for H100 and Blackwell/GB200-class cost-model inputs: achievable framework GEMM throughput, HBM capacity and bandwidth, collective bandwidth by topology, and topology assumptions that affect PP/DP communication costs.

The current report separates measured values from source-backed, inferred, and unknown values. It also records negative results from the JAX/XLA multinode collective harness, including H100 two-node all-gather hangs before the first 1 MB timing record.

## Hypothesis or Goal

Establish a reproducible, evidence-labeled hardware input sheet for the training planner:

- H100 per-GPU achievable bf16/fp8 TFLOP/s and HBM bandwidth.
- Blackwell proxy measurements without mislabeling them as GB200/NVL72 evidence.
- H100 one-node and two-node collective measurements where available.
- GB200/NVL72 topology and public all-reduce anchors, with missing AG/RS measurements marked as unknown.
- Explicit treatment of whether 400 Gb/s scale-out links should be modeled per node or per GPU.

## Status

Current state is usable for H100 all-reduce and partial reduce-scatter modeling, but not complete enough to claim the full requested NCCL matrix.

Measured:

- H100 16k GEMM: 700.6 TFLOP/s bf16 and 1452.7 TFLOP/s fp8_e4m3.
- H100 HBM stream: 2.85 TB/s.
- Blackwell proxy 16k GEMM: 1880.7 TFLOP/s bf16 and 3556.4 TFLOP/s fp8_e4m3.
- Blackwell proxy HBM stream: 6.42 TB/s.
- H100 two-node / 16-rank all-reduce: 364.9 GB/s busbw at 1 GiB.
- H100 two-node / 16-rank reduce-scatter: 277.8 GB/s busbw at 256 MB output chunk.

Unknown or not yet backed by completed measurements:

- Native NCCL all-gather and reduce-scatter on H100 for 1 MB through 1 GiB.
- H100 two-node JAX all-gather; both normal and tiled forms hung before first timing record.
- H100 two-node JAX reduce-scatter at 512 MB and 1 GiB output chunks.
- Any local GB200/NVL72 measurements.
- GB200/NVL72 all-gather and reduce-scatter, intra-rack and inter-rack.
- Fabric oversubscription at larger allocation sizes.

## Links

* Report: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/codex/gpu-hardware-target-report/.agents/reports/gpu-hardware-target-report.md
* Logbook: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/codex/gpu-hardware-target-report/.agents/logbooks/gpu-hardware-target-assumptions.md
* Benchmark harness: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/codex/gpu-hardware-target-report/scripts/bench/gpu_microbench.py
* Snapshot commit: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/commit/b306b74b25
* W&B Report:
* Important updates:

## Decision Log

2026-07-07: Use 700 TFLOP/s bf16, 1250 TFLOP/s fp8, and 2.85 TB/s HBM bandwidth as conservative H100 framework-facing inputs.

2026-07-07: Treat H100 scale-out IB as effectively multi-rail/per-GPU for PP/DP modeling unless an exact provider SKU contradicts it. The measured 365 GB/s two-node all-reduce busbw is not compatible with a single 400 Gb/s NIC per 8-GPU node.

2026-07-07: Do not use the local JAX all-gather numbers as hardware lower bounds. One-node all-gather reports implausibly high busbw after accounting correction, and two-node all-gather hangs before timing.

2026-07-07: Keep Blackwell proxy measurements separate from GB200/NVL72 source-backed values. The current Blackwell proxy is useful for sensitivity studies but is not a local GB200 measurement.

## Conclusion

H100 compute/HBM and H100 all-reduce are sufficiently backed for current planner inputs. Reduce-scatter is partially backed. GB200/NVL72 and all-gather/reduce-scatter native NCCL rows still require dedicated measurements before they should be treated as firm objective inputs.

issues.author: ravwojdyla-agent
issues.body:
## Description

Marin is starting to run long-lived HTTP services on Iris (e.g. `ducky`, an ad-hoc DuckDB SQL service — `lib/ducky`). Iris has no first-class notion of a "service"/"system" job that stays up best-effort across unlimited preemptions and infra failures, and several defaults are footguns for that use case (all code-verified):

- **Retry budgets are lifetime totals that never reset.** `failure_count` / `preemption_count` on the task only ever increment (`lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/reconcile/task.py`); there is no reset for task retry counters anywhere in the controller. Over months of preemptions the budget monotonically climbs to the ceiling and the job goes terminal even if every run lasted days.
- **No "infinite" sentinel.** Enforcement is a plain `count <= max` (`reconcile/task.py:446`, `:208`); `-1` / `0` mean *fewer* retries, so "forever" can only be approximated with a large magic integer.
- **`max_task_failures` defaults to 0 and is a footgun.** It is a job-level cumulative budget: `total_failures > max_task_failures` → `JOB_STATE_FAILED` (`reconcile/job.py:37`). With the default 0, a single hard container failure fails the whole job regardless of `max_retries_failure`. An always-on job that doesn't override it dies on the first OOM/crash.
- **Nothing auto-recreates a terminal/lost job.** No restart policy, no cluster-declared standing-services list the controller reconciles. `existing_job_policy=KEEP` only makes a *client* resubmit idempotent — the controller never resubmits on its own. finelog sidesteps Iris entirely by running as a K8s Deployment with `restartPolicy: Always`.

`ducky` currently works around all of this: an in-process supervisor, `max_retries_{preemption,failure}` and `max_task_failures` all set to `1_000_000`, `existing_job_policy=RECREATE`, and still needs an external watchdog (`ducky deploy --keep` on a schedule) to cover job loss. See `lib/ducky/src/ducky/deploy.py` and `lib/ducky/src/ducky/server.py`.

### Definition of Done

A supported way to declare a long-lived **service job** that:

- retries preemptions/failures effectively forever without per-caller magic numbers — an explicit "unlimited"/restart-policy, or a retry budget that resets after healthy runtime;
- does not die on the first failure by default for the service case (sane `max_task_failures` handling for services);
- is auto-recreated by the cluster if it goes terminal or its state is lost — a declared standing-service list the controller reconciles, or an equivalent — so services don't each need a bespoke external watchdog.

## Related

- #6763 — `IrisDaemon`, the *per-node* (DaemonSet) long-lived-workload primitive. This issue is the *singleton service* (Deployment-equivalent) sibling: one always-on instance, not one-per-node. Both share "a service is a task, inheriting supervision/health/preemption accounting."
- #6722 — service-endpoint leasing (TTL, decoupled from task-row lifetime). Covers the endpoint half of the "survive controller/agent restart" gap noted above.
- #6669 — retry/failure budget field rename. Confirms `max_task_failures` is a job-level cumulative budget changed to *prevent* crash-loop-forever — in direct tension with an always-on service that wants to retry forever. A service primitive should resolve that tension explicitly rather than forcing per-caller `1_000_000` magic numbers.

comments.author: claude[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 **Analysis — not opening a PR (large/design task, no definition of done yet)**

This asks for a *new standalone harness*, not a bug fix. The closest thing today, [`launch_cw_scale.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/grug/moe/launch_cw_scale.py), already env-knobs the model shape and stubs the corpus to SlimPajama-6B — but it is wired through the Marin executor, Fray/Iris `ResourceConfig`, and a real tokenize pipeline, so it is neither standalone nor data-free. A truly shareable repro means decoupling the model + train step from all of that and feeding synthetic tokens.

# Research
**Relevant code**
- [`launch_cw_scale.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/grug/moe/launch_cw_scale.py) — 90B/256-H100 scale launcher; the perf config to mirror
- [`launch.py#L78-L102`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/grug/moe/launch.py#L78-L102) — `slimpajama_6b_data()`; real tokenize step, the data coupling to cut
- [`train.py#L304`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/grug/moe/train.py#L304) — `train_step`; consumes `GrugLmExample` batches via `DataLoader`/`AsyncDataset`
- [`model.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/grug/moe/model.py) — `GrugModelConfig` / `Transformer`
- [`grug_moe.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/grug_moe.py) + [`_moe/ep_deepep.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe/ep_deepep.py) — MoE dispatch / DeepEP GPU expert-parallel backend (the perf-critical path)

Related: #4312 (improve 8×H100 MoE MFU), #6695 (verify CE path in May profile), #6386 (CoreWeave Grug MoE canary scaling).

# Proposed approach (for review before I build it)
A single runnable script (e.g. `experiments/grug/moe/repro_gpu.py`) that:
1. Builds `GrugModelConfig` + the FSDP/expert-parallel mesh exactly as `launch_cw_scale.py` does (reuse `build_scale_model` and the `expert_axis`/`replica_axis` math), but imports **only** Levanter/Haliax/JAX — no `marin.execution`, no Fray/Iris, no executor.
2. Replaces the dataset with an in-process synthetic source yielding random-token `GrugLmExample` batches of the right `[batch, seq]` shape — zero I/O, no tokenize.
3. Runs N steps with the existing `train_step`, warms up past compile, and prints step time / tokens-per-sec / MFU, optionally a `jax_profile` window.

This keeps the perf-critical model + MoE EP code identical to production while removing every dependency an external engineer can't run.

**Decisions I need from you before implementing:**
1. **Target scale** — single 8×H100 node (~9.5B canary class, runs anywhere) or the full 90B/256-GPU multi-node shape? Standalone+shareable argues for single-node by default, multi-node opt-in via env.
2. **"Replicates the GPU performance"** — what's the acceptance metric? Match the real run's step time / MFU within some % at a fixed shape, or just "exercises the same kernels and reports throughput"?
3. **Dependency surface** — strictly Levanter+JAX (so it ships outside this repo), or is "no Marin executor / no Iris, but still inside the marin tree" good enough?

Tell me 1–3 (or just "single-node, throughput-only, inside the tree" and I'll run with it) and I'll open the PR.

comments.author: ravwojdyla-agent
comments.body:
🤖 Standalone GPU MoE repro — working, validated on a single 8×H100 node

Added [`experiments/grug/moe/standalone_repro.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/rav/grug-moe-standalone-6759/experiments/grug/moe/standalone_repro.py) on branch [`rav/grug-moe-standalone-6759`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/rav/grug-moe-standalone-6759) (off `main`). Single-file launcher that runs the production grug MoE train step on synthetic data with **no Marin infra** — no iris/fray dispatch, no GCS/R2 data, no W&B required. Just `python -m experiments.grug.moe.standalone_repro`.

**What it does**
- builds the May `d=2560` shape from `main`'s `GrugModelConfig` (fully CLI-configurable: `--hidden-dim/--num-layers/--num-experts/--top-k/--seq-len/--sliding-window/--moe-impl/--attn-impl/--remat`)
- deterministic in-memory token stream (`SyntheticGrugDataset`, ported from the `codex/deepep-*` branch) — zero data I/O, optional periodic EOS + packed `segment_ids`
- builds the compact `(replica_dcn, data, expert, model)` mesh and calls the in-process `_run_grug_local` directly (the same entry each Fray worker runs) — so it needs no dispatch layer
- mesh configurable; **defaults to 2×8×H100** (`--expert-axis 8`, replica = `jax.process_count()`)
- profiling: rank-0 xprof trace logged as a **W&B artifact** under `--wandb`; opt-in `--perfetto-trace` also bundles the perfetto trace (ui.perfetto.dev)

**Validated on 1×8×H100 (`cw-us-east-02a`)** — mirrors the codex single-node `GM2560-…-N1` shape (2 layers / 256 experts):
- run `GM2560-STANDALONE-L2-E8-B8-EOS512-N1-cw-20260701-001025` — finished 30/30 steps, fail=0
- 5.75B params (d2560, 2 layers, 256 experts top-4, seq 4096); E8M1 8-process multi-controller
- loss 1.43 → 1.12; **MFU ~5.5** (p50 5.52); **145K tok/s**; `ring` MoE + `gpu_fa4_cute` + `save_moe`
- xprof trace (steps 8–15) captured on rank 0 and logged as a W&B artifact
- the standalone auto-detected the Iris job context and initialized `jax.distributed` with **no code changes** (same `_run_grug_local` as production)

**Gotchas found running on the iris GPU path** (all worth documenting):
1. `gpu_fa4_cute` requires packed `segment_ids` — run synthetic data with `--eos-interval > 0`; a plain causal mask (`eos_interval=0`) is rejected with `NotImplementedError: … requires packed segment_ids`.
2. iris defaults `JAX_COMPILATION_CACHE_DIR` to `s3://…/compilation-cache`, and XLA's per-fusion autotune sub-cache has no `s3://` filesystem driver → `UNIMPLEMENTED: File system scheme 's3'`. Fix: pass a local `JAX_COMPILATION_CACHE_DIR` (iris respects an explicit setting). Only bites on the iris path, not an external box.
3. levanter's profiler wrote a perfetto trace on **every** rank and barriered across all ranks — the concurrent perfetto write corrupted/hung (`BadGzipFile`) at 8 ranks. Fixed by adding `create_perfetto_trace` + `profile_process_index` to `ProfilerConfig` (defaults preserve behavior): profile rank 0 only, keep the stop barrier on all ranks. The standalone profiles rank 0 with perfetto off by default.

MFU ~5.5 is expected for this smoke shape (batch 8 = 1/device, only 2 layers → overhead-dominated, `Adam` not `muonh`); scaling layers/batch or switching to muonh raises it. Full `d2560` (26 layers / 256 experts) won't fit one node — it was sized for 32.

Branch is pushed (`rav/grug-moe-standalone-6759`, 3 commits); PR against `main` next.

issues.author: rjpower
issues.body:
## Summary

Construct the output-path-dependent training config fields in `train_lm`'s `build_config(ctx)` instead of baking them into a blank config later, on the worker, at run time. Retire `bake_output_path` / `_update_config_to_use_out_path` and the separate `output_path` field threading. This is leftover from the old executor framework and is now pure indirection under the lazy `ArtifactStep` model.

## Current shape (config built blank, mutated later, on a different machine)

1. **Coordinator** — `train_lm`'s `build_config(ctx)` (`lib/marin/src/marin/experiment/train.py:131-171`) builds a `TrainLmOnPodConfig` whose inner `TrainLmConfig` has the checkpointer at its *default* base path, `hf_save_path=None`, and `trainer.id` possibly `None`. The real output dir is **not** baked in — it is carried alongside as a separate `output_path=ctx.output_path` field.
2. **Worker** — `run_levanter_train_lm` → `_prepare_training_run` (`lib/marin/src/marin/training/training.py:490-522`) then calls `_update_config_to_use_out_path` → `bake_output_path`, a cascade of `dataclasses.replace` that injects `checkpointer.base_path = <out>/checkpoints`, `temporary_base_path`, and `hf_save_path = <out>/hf`; plus `_enforce_run_id` imputing `trainer.id` from `basename(output_path)`, a cpu `require_accelerator` toggle, and `doublecheck_paths`.

So the config is *constructed* in one place and its path-dependent fields are *filled in* in another, on a different machine, at run time.

## Why it exists (and why it's now obsolete)

The docstring says it outright (`_update_config_to_use_out_path`, `training.py:258`): _"useful when running with the executor framework, where the output path is set by the executor."_ In the **old** executor model, steps were built at **import time**, before the executor assigned the content-hash output path (`name-<hash>`) — the path did not exist at construction, so it had to be baked in late, on the worker, right before launch.

Under the lazy model `build_config(ctx)` runs with `ctx.output_path` already resolved (`{prefix}/{name}/{version}`), so the config can be constructed correctly up front. Verified: `bake_output_path` is a **pure function of `(train_config, output_path)`** with no worker-side dependency — even the region-local temp goes through `marin_temp_bucket(source_prefix=output_path)` (`lib/rigging/src/rigging/filesystem.py:341`), which derives the region from the **output path**, not the worker VM region. Run-id imputation is just `basename(output_path)`, and the cpu toggle depends only on `resources` — both build-time-knowable.

## Proposed change

- Build the full `TrainerConfig` in `build_config(ctx)` with the real `checkpointer.base_path`, `temporary_base_path`, `hf_save_path` (see #6752 re: dropping the forced HF path), and `trainer.id` — directly from `ctx.output_path`.
- Keep on the worker only what is genuinely run-time:
  - `resolve_training_env` — assembling env vars (GIT_COMMIT, WANDB, JAX compilation-cache dir, accel defaults) and applying them to `os.environ` for levanter;
  - `doublecheck_paths` — the runtime check that configured GCS paths match the live VM region.
- Delete `bake_output_path`, `_update_config_to_use_out_path`, the separate `output_path` field threading, and the run-id-from-output-path imputation; replace "build blank, mutate later" with "build it right once."

## Relationship to #6752

#6752 (HF export as a separate `export_hf` step) wants HF export out of `bake_output_path` anyway. This cleanup naturally removes the forced `hf_save_path` assignment; coordinate the two so the HF path is dropped here and re-introduced as its own step there.

## Blast radius

`_prepare_training_run` is shared by LM **and** DPO (`run_levanter_train_lm` / `run_levanter_train_dpo`) and feeds many experiments; `bake_output_path` / `impute_run_id` are also used by other call sites. This is a real refactor of the shared training entry, not a drop-in — it was not required to make the new steps *run*, only to make them clean.

## Key references

- `lib/marin/src/marin/training/training.py:176-200` — `bake_output_path`
- `lib/marin/src/marin/training/training.py:249-272` — `_update_config_to_use_out_path` (docstring naming the executor-framework origin at `:258`)
- `lib/marin/src/marin/training/training.py:203-246` — `impute_run_id` / `:403` `_enforce_run_id`
- `lib/marin/src/marin/training/training.py:490-522` — `_prepare_training_run` (shared LM/DPO)
- `lib/marin/src/marin/experiment/train.py:131-171` — `build_config` that already has `ctx.output_path`
- `lib/rigging/src/rigging/filesystem.py:341` — `marin_temp_bucket(source_prefix=...)` (region from output path, not VM)

_Filed from the lazy ArtifactStep / executor-context adoption work; surfaced while reviewing the training config path._

comments.author: claude[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 **Plan:**
- [x] Read issue + duplicate-work preflight
- [x] Verify technical claims against the code
- [x] Post analysis (no PR — large refactor on unmerged code)

# Research

Proposal is **sound and verified**, but this is a refactor of the shared LM/DPO training entry (>100 lines, the issue says so itself), and — critically — **the code it targets does not exist on `main`.** `experiment/train.py`, `build_config(ctx)`, and `ctx.output_path` live only in the branch of #6649 ([`weaver/adopt-executor-context-for-remai`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/6649), still OPEN). The issue's line refs match that branch exactly (`build_config` at `train.py:131`, `bake_output_path` at `training.py:176`, `_update_config_to_use_out_path` at `:249`). So this is **stacked-on-#6649 cleanup**, not a `main` change. Per scope rules I'm posting analysis rather than a PR.

Claims I confirmed:
- `bake_output_path` **is** a pure fn of `(train_config, output_path)` — no worker/VM dependency (`training.py:176-200`, branch).
- Region-local temp comes from the **output path**, not the VM: `marin_temp_bucket(source_prefix=...)` — *"An explicit source_prefix fully determines the backend and region"* ([`filesystem.py:378-385`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/rigging/src/rigging/filesystem.py#L378-L385)).
- Run-id imputation case 4 is `basename(output_path)`; cpu `require_accelerator` toggle depends only on `resources`, which `build_config` already has via `ctx.runtime_arg("train_resources")` (`train.py:168`). Both build-time-knowable. ✔

# Proposed approach (for #6649 author)

The build-time / run-time split the issue describes is correct. **Build-time** (move into `build_config(ctx)`): `bake_output_path` (base_path, temporary_base_path, hf_save_path), run-id, cpu toggle, `_maybe_override_auto_build_caches`. **Run-time, keep on worker**: `resolve_training_env` (GIT_COMMIT/WANDB/JAX cache — its `marin_temp_bucket` call has **no** `source_prefix`, so it's genuinely launcher/region-dependent, `training.py:480-484`) and `doublecheck_paths` (live VM-region check).

Three nuances the "it's just `bake_output_path` + run-id" framing misses — handle these in the move, don't drop them:

1. **Adapter/PEFT path rewrite.** `_update_config_to_use_out_path` also nulls `hf_save_path` and sets `peft_save_path` for adapter LM/DPO (`training.py:265-270`, branch). Pure, so it moves to `build_config` too — but it must move *with* the hf-path logic, and this is exactly the seam #6752 (separate `export_hf` step) wants to cut. Coordinate: drop the forced `hf_save_path` here, reintroduce as its own step there.
2. **Run-id precedence changes.** `impute_run_id` priority is `trainer.id` → `env_vars["RUN_ID"]` → `os.environ["RUN_ID"]` → `basename(output_path)` (`training.py:203-246`). `build_config` already passes `id=run_id` (`train.py:138`), so build-time imputation is usually a no-op — but moving it build-time means a worker-side `RUN_ID` **env var no longer overrides**. Confirm nothing relies on that (Iris/ferry-injected `RUN_ID`).
3. **DPO auto-schedule reads tokenizer stats.** `_maybe_auto_resolve_dpo_schedule` → `_dpo_training_dataset_size` does I/O (`training.py:303-305`). Decide explicitly whether it stays worker-side or moves; it is *not* a pure config transform like the rest.

Net: `_prepare_training_run` shrinks to `resolve_training_env` + `_apply_env_to_process` + `doublecheck_paths`; `bake_output_path` / `_update_config_to_use_out_path` / `_enforce_run_id` / the separate `output_path` field thread get deleted. Land it as a follow-up commit on #6649 (or a PR stacked on it), gated on the #6752 hf-export decision.

comments.author: rjpower
comments.body:
🤖 Revisited now that the lazy ArtifactStep work (#6649) has landed. Opened #6809 for the cleanup, but with a correction to this issue's proposed mechanism.

**The cleaner way already exists in-tree.** The grug base/moe launchers build their checkpointer paths directly from `output_path` and never touch `bake_output_path`. `train_lm` was the last holdout on the blank-config-then-`dataclasses.replace`-cascade. So the fix is to make `train_lm` match grug and delete the cascade — no new machinery.

**But building the paths inside `build_config(ctx)` (as this issue proposes) is subtly wrong.** `build_config` runs at *fingerprint* time too, with `ctx.output_path == "<output_path>"`. Two consequences the earlier analysis missed:

1. **Region leak into identity.** `temporary_checkpoint_base_path("<output_path>")` → `marin_temp_bucket` can't parse a region from the placeholder, so it falls through to `marin_prefix()` and bakes the *ambient cluster's root* into the fingerprint. Identity would then depend on which cluster you lowered from. (The earlier comment's claim that the temp path is "build-time-knowable and pure" holds for the VM, but not for the fingerprint placeholder.)
2. **Fingerprint churn.** Moving `base_path` into `build_config` changes the fingerprinted value from the default `"checkpoints/"` to `"<output_path>/checkpoints"` — a new hash for every existing train artifact, forcing TPU recompute of cached fixed-version runs.

Grug sidesteps both by keeping path construction in its `run` callable (real `output_path`, after fingerprinting). #6809 does the same for `train_lm`: it deletes `bake_output_path` / `_update_config_to_use_out_path` / `impute_run_id` / `_enforce_run_id` and replaces them with direct construction (`resolve_checkpointer_output_path` + `apply_output_path` + `_resolve_run_id`, the first now shared with grug), while leaving the fingerprint byte-for-byte unchanged.

Scope notes: DPO isn't wired into the lazy layer yet (no `TrainDpoOnPodConfig` constructor in production), so `_prepare_training_run` is shared but only `train_lm` exercised the cascade. The forced `hf_save_path` is preserved for now — dropping it belongs with #6752's separate `export_hf` step, not this structural cleanup.

issues.author: dlwh
issues.body:
## Candidate-9 result (2026-09-29): sweep complete

The matched candidate-9 test records no final pure-EMA Paloma win over its same-seed controls at d512 or d768. Mean losses are:

| Arm | d512 | d768 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Control | 2.98053 | 2.72219 |
| Standard α=1 | 2.99639 (+0.01586) | 2.73433 (+0.01214) |
| α=1, coda warmup | 2.99379 (+0.01325) | 2.73282 (+0.01063), seed0 repeat |
| α=1, preserve bigram selection | 2.98831 (+0.00777) | 2.72487 (+0.00268) |

Parentheses give loss minus the matched control; lower is better. Preservation recovers most of standard α=1's penalty at both widths but remains worse on both seeds; it is a persistent source-selection change with unchanged parameter shapes. Recorded midpoint/final evaluations and sampled late training windows do not show the hypothesized late win. These runs modify the inherited candidate-9 recipe; no full BO-specific hyperparameter search or dense-Transformer replication was performed. Pause this line after the authorized sweep; no further runs are planned. [Final seed-paired results, learning windows, throughput and provenance](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9280#issuecomment-5901009948).

The one authorized unchanged d768 warmup seed0 repeat completed all 7325 updates and evaluations on Iris/W&B. It passed the original NaN step 5441 with finite loss and finished at Paloma 2.73488. This shows nonrecurrence in one attempt; the original failure cause remains unknown. Its paired mean uses the successful repeat with original seed1 and is conditioned on completion. Original d768 α=.707 seed0 failed at 1532 and was not retried; seed1 finished at 2.73111, so no two-seed final mean exists for that arm. Standard d512 α=1 seed0 completed training/evaluation, then failed during tracker shutdown; its primary score is saved and blend scores are unavailable. All authorized attempts are now terminal and the monitor is stopped. [Failures](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9280#issuecomment-5899790837), [repeat authorization and recipe](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9280#issuecomment-5899890438).

Earlier May-ladder loss wins below remain confounded by attention-window semantics. [d512 detailed results](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9280#issuecomment-5899525010), [standard d768](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9280#issuecomment-5900079796), [preservation d768](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9280#issuecomment-5900468443).

## Goal

Test the boundary operator from [arXiv 2609.19107](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.19107) ("How Model Growth, Recursion, and Boundary Operators Influence Scaling Exponents") on the grug MoE block, at matched parameters and FLOPs, before building any of the paper's looping/growth machinery.

The operator (paper's Operator-1, K=1, no looping, no growth): split the layers into prelude/core/coda (as even as possible; remainders to core first, then coda). The core starts from `h₀ = 0`, so its entry state is `BO(0, e) = α·e` where `e` is the prelude's output; after the last core block, the coda's entry state is `BO(h, e) = rms_norm(h) + α·e`. One RMSNorm and two vector-adds; zero new parameters.

Why this first: the paper reports the operator alone (no recursion, no growth) already moves the scaling exponent — effective compute multiplier ≈1.25× at 1e20 FLOPs. It is the cheapest decisive test of whether the paper's axes transfer to the MoE template: if the operator doesn't move the grug isoflop curves, looping/growth almost certainly won't either.

## Plan

- Variant `experiments/grug/moe_boundary/` copied from `experiments/grug/moe/` (copy-first per the grug archive workflow). Boundary-off is byte-identical to the parent (regression-tested on logits).
- Phase 0 arms at the four May Recipe compute-optimal cells (d512/3.82e17, d768/2.81e18, d1024/1.16e19, d1280/3.46e19), v4-32 EP=1, with the README measurement conditions pinned (seq 4096, PKO on, long RoPE on, z-loss off, batch/steps from the README table).
- d512 runs both α ∈ {1.0, 0.707} ("alpha insurance"; paper's tuned values for Operator-1 and Loop-2). Winner by final macro loss proceeds.
- Gate 1: effective speedup > 1 at d512 and d768 vs the README baselines (3.5422 @ 433,986 tok/s; 3.2273 @ 294,726).
- Gate 2: d1024 + d1280, refit `loss(C) = 1.6 + A·C^−α̂`, projections must beat 2.534 @ 1e21 and 2.205 @ 1e23; fitted α̂ vs 0.0941 is secondary evidence.
- Cost: ≈45 v4-32 slice-hours for the full phase; ≈7–8 for gate 1 alone.

## Records

Runs land in W&B project `marin_moe`, group `moe-boundary`. Results and the go/no-go call get recorded here as each gate resolves.

**Final outcome (2026-09-29, matched recipe):** the measured loss wins at all four cells are confounded by an attention-window semantics change between the June baselines and the September variant runs, so the Phase 0 loss/speedup readout below is exploratory, not gate-grade. The one unconfounded result is throughput parity: the boundary operator costs ~0% at every scale (d1280 same-stack, same-window variant vs probe: 160,661 vs 160,924 tok/s, −0.16%).

The June 4 baselines ran short/long windows of 1024/2048 tokens (June code: `short = cfg.sliding_window // 2`, `long = cfg.sliding_window`, long rule `i % 4 == 3`), while the September variant runs used the current semantics — short 2048, long full-context, plus the last-layer long rule. Both eras log `sliding_window=2048`, so config matching did not catch it. Correcting for the window pattern, the September variant arms ran ~10% more real attention compute per token than the June baselines at every cell. Via the baseline law, that alone implies a loss win larger than the variant's measured wins, so the operator's measured Δloss cannot be separated from the window confound without a matched-window rerun.

| cell | variant macro | baseline macro | measured Δloss | window-implied Δloss | speedup (confounded) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| d512 3.82e17 | 3.5415 | 3.5422 | −0.0007 | −0.0179 | 1.005 |
| d768 2.81e18 | 3.2186 | 3.2273 | −0.0087 | −0.0136 | 1.050 |
| d1024 1.16e19 | 3.0129 | 3.0195 | −0.0066 | −0.0136 | 1.061 |
| d1280 3.46e19 | 2.8792 | 2.8857 | −0.0065 | −0.0120 | 1.054 |

- Gate 1 was recorded as passing; under the window confound that readout is exploratory. Gate 2's projection refit is equally confounded (the variant cells sit at higher real compute than the baseline law fit).
- α=1.0 beat α=0.707 at d512 (3.5415 vs 3.5459) — a within-era comparison; unaffected by the confound.
- The earlier "jax 0.9.2 → 0.11.1 stack drift" attribution for the d1280 throughput gap is retracted: controlled jax-version probes differ by 0.07%. The gap is now attributed to the window semantics change (#9529); a same-stack June-window probe is queued to quantify it.
- Measurement notes: throughput figures are per-step medians (last-200-step averages are contaminated by end-of-run degradation).
- Training curves: [d1280 matched-pair report](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/reports/moe_boundary-d1280-matched-pair:-variant-vs-baseline--VmlldzoxODAyMDY5MQ==); variant runs `moe_boundary_compute_opt_d{512,768,1024,1280}_ep1_alpha1_matched`; June baselines `moe_may_compute_opt_d{512,768,1024,1280}_ep1`.
- Result table and methodology live in `experiments/grug/moe_boundary/README.md`. Next steps: matched-window rerun (variant and baseline on identical window semantics) before any promotion decision.

Part of #4281.

comments.author: claude[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 **Analysis — scope: research experiment, no PR yet**

This is a multi-cell training experiment (variant + four v4-32 isoflop cells, two go/no-go gates, W&B recording), not a self-contained code fix. The workflow reserves PRs for small self-contained changes; larger/experiment work gets a reviewed approach first. Below is the grounded implementation design for the *code scaffolding* (the variant); launching the runs and resolving the gates is operator work (`use-iris` / grug launchers), not part of a code PR.

**Where the operator slots in.** The MoE forward loop iterates blocks linearly at [`model.py` L685–707](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/7b63e0d0cefcb19282fd9cc7efb3c109cbfc4801/experiments/grug/moe/model.py#L685-L707). Operator-1 (K=1, no loop/growth) wraps that loop:
- Split `self.blocks` into prelude / core / coda — even split, remainders to core first then coda.
- Run prelude on `hidden`; save `e = hidden` (prelude output).
- Core entry state `BO(0, e) = α·e` (core starts from `h₀=0`), so feed `α·e` into the first core block.
- After the last core block, coda entry state `BO(h, e) = rms_norm(h) + α·e`.
- Coda runs normally, then `final_norm` / `final_gated_norm` as today.

**Zero new parameters.** The paper's single RMSNorm is the existing non-parametric [`rms_norm` free function (`model.py` L252)](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/7b63e0d0cefcb19282fd9cc7efb3c109cbfc4801/experiments/grug/moe/model.py#L252) — reuse it; do not add an `RMSNorm` module. The two adds are plain vector adds.

**Config knobs.** Add to `GrugModelConfig` ([`model.py` L95–133](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/7b63e0d0cefcb19282fd9cc7efb3c109cbfc4801/experiments/grug/moe/model.py#L95-L133)) a single `boundary_alpha: float | None = None`. `None` ⇒ boundary off ⇒ the forward path must be byte-identical to the parent (the "boundary-off" regression baseline the issue asks for). Set `0.707` (1/√2) or `1.0` to enable. Avoid a separate boolean + float pair (compound-state anti-pattern per AGENTS.md).

**Variant location.** Copy `experiments/grug/moe/` → `experiments/grug/moe_boundary/` (copy-first, per `change-grug` / grug archive workflow; the issue's own plan agrees). Keep edits local; no shared framework surface. Add a `docs/reports/grug-archive.md` entry (origin `moe`, purpose, status `active`, diff link from the CI diff comment).

**Test that earns its place.** One regression test: with `boundary_alpha=None`, logits are bitwise-equal to the parent `moe` model on a fixed seed/input (the issue's "byte-identical" claim). Optionally a shape/finiteness check with `boundary_alpha=0.707`. No tautological tests.

**Open questions before coding:**
1. Per-cell `num_layers` for d512/d768/d1024/d1280 come from the May Recipe README table — confirm the exact counts so the even prelude/core/coda split is well-defined (e.g. how a 6-layer cell splits: 2/2/2).
2. Confirm the split is by *block index* only (the attention long/short pattern at L688–690 stays keyed to absolute layer index `i`, unchanged by the operator).
3. Should `boundary_alpha` also thread through the HF config round-trip (`to_hf_config`/`from_hf_config`), or stay experiment-only? Recommend experiment-only until it proves out.

I can implement the variant + regression test as a scoped PR on request (code only; runs excluded). Want me to proceed with that, or adjust the design first?
