comments.author: claude[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 **Actionable as a design proposal, not a PR.** This is a new CI-triggered deploy capability touching production infra with real trigger/safety design choices (which services, what triggers a redeploy, rollback), so posting analysis + proposed approach for review rather than a unilateral PR.

# Research

Both services already have mature deploy CLIs; what's missing is a CI job that runs them after a build/test passes. There's already a working precedent for CI-driven deploys with GCP auth.

- **finelog** deploys to a GCE VM running `ghcr.io/marin-community/finelog:latest`; restart re-pulls the image. Safe path with health-check + rollback exists.
- **ducky** is an always-on Iris TPU job; redeploy is an idempotent `--keep` watchdog submit that needs a controller tunnel.
- CI already does this pattern for the Iris controller (GCP SA auth, ephemeral OS Login SSH, run the CLI), triggered by cron + manual — no `workflow_run`-on-success deploy exists anywhere.

**Relevant code**
- [`iris-dev-restart.yaml`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/.github/workflows/iris-dev-restart.yaml) — existing CI deploy pattern to copy (SA auth + OS Login + CLI restart)
- [`finelog/scripts/safe_deploy.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/finelog/scripts/safe_deploy.py) — `rollout`/`rollback` with health check; digest cached for rollback
- [`finelog/deploy/_gcp.py#L189`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/finelog/src/finelog/deploy/_gcp.py#L189) — `gcp_restart()` (`finelog deploy restart marin`)
- [`ducky/deploy.py#L67`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/ducky/src/ducky/deploy.py#L67) — `submit_ducky()`; `ducky deploy --cluster marin --keep`, auto-tunnels, region-pinned TPU job
- [`ops-docker-images.yaml#L100-L109`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/.github/workflows/ops-docker-images.yaml#L100) — builds/pushes `finelog:latest` (weekly + dispatch); the natural upstream to gate finelog redeploy

# Proposed approach (design)

Add one deploy workflow per service, cloning the `iris-dev-restart.yaml` scaffold (checkout → `google-github-actions/auth` with `IRIS_CI_GCP_SA_KEY` → ephemeral OS Login SSH → run CLI → remove key). As services multiply, factor the auth+OS-Login boilerplate into a composite action under `.github/actions/` so each new service is ~15 lines. Both start with `workflow_dispatch` so they can be exercised manually before any auto-trigger is armed.

**finelog** — trigger via `workflow_run` on **Ops - Docker Images** completing successfully (that's what publishes `:latest`; restarting on merges that don't rebuild the image is pointless). Deploy step uses `safe_deploy.py rollout marin`, not raw `deploy restart`, so a bad image auto-rolls-back on health-check failure. This is genuinely small and low-risk.

**ducky** — heavier: needs a controller tunnel and submits a TPU job, and `--keep` is a no-op when the job is already healthy (only picks up new code on job restart). Suggest a separate, later workflow (or scheduled `--keep` watchdog) gated on `Ducky - Unit` success on `main`; worth its own discussion before wiring.

**Open questions for reviewers:**
1. Trigger model — `workflow_run` on the upstream build/test, or `push: branches:[main]` with `paths:` scoped to the service dir? I lean `workflow_run` so we only deploy artifacts CI actually validated.
2. Redeploy cadence — event-driven per merge, or keep it a daily scheduled refresh like `iris-dev-restart`? Per-merge finelog restarts are cheap; per-merge ducky TPU-job churn may not be desirable.
3. Should finelog redeploy always go through `safe_deploy.py` (rollback) — I assume yes.

If the trigger model + safety story above is agreed, I'll open the finelog workflow first (small, self-contained) and follow with ducky separately. cc @rjpower

spillover_issues.author: rjpower
spillover_issues.body:
We want to introduce a workflow to allow external submissions to the Marin/Iris cluster.

This will allow a broader set of users to contribute to Marin experiments and for us to validate without requiring manual intervention to check out branches and execute experiments manually. It also encourages us to better "package" experiments, so that, for example, the top-level experiment file encapsulates all Iris client operations, instead of the current approach which requires users to run `uv run iris` to boot applications (a common area of complaints).

As a incremental step, let's adjust our existing Grug/Dupekit examples to handle the Iris launching themselves, and add a workflow for trusted users which triggers an agent to run the given experiment on an Iris cluster.

comments.author: claude[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 **Plan:**
- [x] Read issue, AGENTS.md, fix-issue and author-pr skills
- [x] Survey current grug/datakit launch flow and existing GitHub workflows
- [x] Decide scope: multi-module feature + workflow + design choices — too large for an auto-PR
- [x] Post research + proposed approach for human review (no PR)

**Research**

Two distinct asks:

1. **Self-launching experiments** — today `python -m experiments.grug.base.launch` (or `datakit_testbed/train.py`) just builds configs; the Iris submission has to be wrapped externally by `uv run iris --cluster=marin job run --extra=cpu -- python -m experiments.X`. `train_grug` already calls [`_submit_train_job`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/defaults.py#L555-L588), which calls `current_client()`. That `current_client()` only resolves to a real cluster when an `IrisContext` is already in scope — which is what `uv run iris job run` sets up. Letting the launch script run end-to-end from a plain `python …/launch.py` means each launch needs to open its own `IrisClient.remote(...)` + `iris_ctx_scope(...)` (see [`client.py#L481-L516`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/client/client.py#L481-L516), [`client.py#L1109-L1120`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/client/client.py#L1109-L1120)) before invoking the existing entrypoint. Datakit testbed has the same shape via `executor_main` over `run_testbed_trial` steps.

2. **GitHub submission workflow** — `.github/workflows/marin-canary-ferry.yaml` already shows the GCP-auth + `.venv/bin/iris job run --no-wait` + `scripts/workflows/iris_monitor.py wait/collect` recipe for a single hard-coded experiment. `ops-claude.yaml` shows the trusted-user gate (`author_association in (OWNER, MEMBER, COLLABORATOR)`). What is missing is a parameterized workflow that accepts an experiment path (PR comment / `workflow_dispatch` input) and submits *that* experiment, gated on the same association check.

**Relevant code**
- [`experiments/grug/base/launch.py#L169-L252`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/grug/base/launch.py#L169-L252) — current `__main__` calls `train_grug` but requires `iris job run` wrapper
- [`experiments/grug/README.md#L40-L48`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/grug/README.md#L40-L48) — documents the current `uv run iris ... -- python -m …` boilerplate users complain about
- [`experiments/defaults.py#L555-L588`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/defaults.py#L555-L588) — `_submit_train_job` / `current_client()` dependency
- [`lib/iris/config/marin.yaml`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/config/marin.yaml) — production cluster config the workflow needs to pick up
- [`.github/workflows/marin-canary-ferry.yaml#L38-L100`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/.github/workflows/marin-canary-ferry.yaml#L38-L100) — template for GCP auth + iris submission in CI
- [`.github/workflows/ops-claude.yaml#L17-L36`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/.github/workflows/ops-claude.yaml#L17-L36) — `author_association` trusted-user gate
- [`scripts/workflows/iris_monitor.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/scripts/workflows/iris_monitor.py) — reusable `wait` + `collect` monitoring

**Proposed Approach (for review — not implementing yet)**

*Step 1: introduce a small `experiments/_launch.py` helper.*

```python
# experiments/_launch.py
def with_iris(fn, *, cluster: str = "marin", controller: str | None = None,
              workspace: Path | None = None) -> None:
    """Open an IrisClient + ctx and invoke fn() under it.

    Resolves controller address from IRIS_CONTROLLER_ADDRESS env var (set
    by `iris job run`) or by reading lib/iris/config/<cluster>.yaml.
    No-op if an IrisContext is already in scope — keeps `iris job run -- ...`
    backwards-compatible for the ferry workflows.
    """
```

Then each variant's `__main__` becomes:

```python
if __name__ == "__main__":
    from experiments._launch import with_iris
    with_iris(lambda: train_grug(name="grug/base-trial", launch=grug_base_launch))
```

Only the targets called out in the issue change in this increment: `experiments/grug/base/launch.py`, `experiments/grug/moe/launch.py`, and `experiments/datakit_testbed/train.py` (it already wraps `executor_main`; just gain the same `with_iris` wrap on its `__main__`). The README's "Iris cluster run" snippet collapses to `uv run python experiments/grug/base/launch.py`.

*Step 2: add `.github/workflows/ops-run-experiment.yaml`.*

- Trigger: `issue_comment` on PRs/issues with body starting `/run-experiment <path>` AND `author_association ∈ {OWNER, MEMBER, COLLABORATOR}` (mirror `ops-claude.yaml`).
- Parse the path with a tiny inline script; reject anything not under `experiments/`.
- Steps follow `marin-canary-ferry.yaml`: GCP auth → SSH key → `.venv/bin/iris --config=$IRIS_CONFIG job run --no-wait --extra=cpu -- python -m <module>` → `iris_monitor.py wait` → `iris_monitor.py collect`.
- Post status + W&B link back as a single PR comment (`gh pr comment --edit-last`).
- Reuse the existing `IRIS_CI_GCP_SA_KEY` / `IRIS_CI_GCP_SSH_KEY` secrets.

**Design questions to resolve before implementation**

1. Trust model: collaborator association is the same gate as `@claude`. Good enough for "trusted users" the issue mentions, or do we want a separate allowlist file?
2. Branch ref: the workflow should check out `github.event.issue.pull_request` head SHA for PR comments, and `main` for issue comments. Confirm both are in scope.
3. Resource cap: should we constrain `--reserve` to a per-comment allowlist (e.g. `v5p-8` only) to bound cost, similar to canary jobs?
4. Concurrency: `concurrency.group: run-experiment-${{ github.event.issue.number }}` to prevent double-submits on quick repeated comments?
5. Scope of Step 1: just the three files above, or also sweep every `experiments/*/launch.py` that has the boilerplate? The issue says "incremental step" — recommend the three.

Will not open a PR until these are answered. ~250 LOC across helper + workflow once Q1–Q5 land.

spillover_issues.author: hammer
spillover_issues.body:
The [Arcee Trinity Large Technical Report](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.17004) in Section 3.2 Data Preparation defines a metric, Batch Heterogeneity, (BatchHet), that tracks the difference between the maximum microbatch loss and the average loss for each training step, and claim that this metric correlates strongly with gradient norm instability. They note that, as models grow larger, their step-to-step data efficiency tends to increase, and hypothesize that makes them more vulnerable to the step-to-step fluctuations in the data distribution, which causes training instability as models grow larger.

They introduce a method, the Random Sequential Document Buffer (RSDB), to reduce this metric. I'm not sure that method is useful for us as I don't believe we do on-the-fly tokenization. 

Should we track this metric? Given some of the [spikes](https://discord.com/channels/1354881461060243556/1375005693899309126/1479363883813830717) we saw with Delphi that were related to bad data, I have been having bouts of anxiety about some weird data-related training instability hit late in a hero run due to unfortunate sampling packing bad data together in unforeseen ways and have been thinking about how we could mitigate that risk. Adding this metric, creating data that causes it to spike, and developing methods to reduce it even in the face of bad data seems potentially interesting?

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖
# Research

Marin currently launches the external MarinSkyRL trainer through `skyrl_step()` and runs Harbor evaluations through a separate runner; this checkout has no `TaskSpec` or `RolloutEngine` implementation. MarinSkyRL [#712](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/pull/712) already drafts native generation for stateless assistant-final tasks and Harbor execution for stateful tasks, but it is pinned to an older TaskCompendium spike and is waiting for the current package interfaces. The existing SkyRL [rollout-buffer contract](https://echo.oa.dev/wiki/521) provides producer writes, typed receipts, trainer admission, and checkpoint snapshots, so the engine should use that handoff.

**Relevant code**
- [`skyrl.py#L270-L356`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/marin/src/marin/rl/skyrl.py#L270-L356) — Marin's external training launcher.
- [`runner.py#L239-L282`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/harbor/runner.py#L239-L282) — separate Harbor evaluation loop.
- [MarinSkyRL #712](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/pull/712) — draft TaskCompendium dispatch.
- [TaskCompendium grading in #9608](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9608/files) — submission and verifier contract.
- [TaskCompendium providers in #9522](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9522/files) — stateful tool execution contract.

# Rollout Engine proposal

A single `RolloutEngine.run(buffer)` should own task admission, policy-version selection, execution, grading, and the write to the existing `RolloutBuffer`. It consumes versioned `TaskSpec` values from a `DataGenerator`, uses the training policy for rollout identity and the inference policy for generation, and emits one typed result per task or reward group. The execution environment selects native chat only when the task can preserve generated token IDs and behavior logprobs; tasks needing tools, workspace state, multi-step context, or non-assistant submissions use Harbor, following #712. Harbor's reconstructed tokens must remain ineligible for objectives requiring exact behavior-policy evidence.

Implementation sequence:

1. Reconcile the issue's `rollout.py` and `environment.py` work with the current TaskCompendium PR stack: typed submissions and grading in [#9608](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9608), stateful providers in [#9522](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9522), and isolated provider execution in [#9607](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9607). Pin one package schema and update #712's old dependency before changing trainer dispatch.
2. Introduce the engine contract at the TaskCompendium/SkyRL boundary. Keep execution backends behind one task-to-result interface, and keep scheduling, capacity limits, policy-step tagging, and buffer commits in the engine. Reuse `RolloutWriter`/`RolloutBuffer`; do not create another durable queue.
3. Preserve grading and failure semantics across backends: invalid final submissions receive zero reward, infrastructure failures have no reward, and only completed graded records enter the buffer. Retain task ID, policy step, token evidence, tool observations, and verifier outcome in the record needed for replay and diagnosis.
4. Replace the four trainer rollout entrypaths only after the new path passes parity checks. Test native exact-token/logprob evidence, a stateful Harbor tool task, invalid versus infrastructure failures, duplicate/retry behavior, and buffer snapshot/restart. Then run a bounded mixed-task, one-step training smoke against the [existing recipe in #9527](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9527), checking completed groups, reward counts, and a committed optimizer step.

Costs and risks: the TaskCompendium interfaces and #712 are still under review, and Harbor trajectories lack exact behavior logprobs. Preserve the existing fail-fast eligibility check until that evidence changes. This session could not read the two linked Google Docs (HTTP 401), and `rollout-engine` is not a published branch in `marin-community/marin`; confirm those sources and the final module placement before implementation. No parallel engine PR is warranted while #712 owns the rollout dispatch work.

Open questions for the owner: Should the engine live in TaskCompendium or MarinSkyRL, with the other package supplying an adapter? Which of the four existing SkyRL paths must be removed in the first landing, and which need a staged migration?

spillover_issues.body:
This issue tracks iterative improvements to the Marin pretraining scaling ladder (`experiments/grug/fast_track`) using the **Marin Belay** process. It is a twist on autoresearch: an agent runs experiments in batches, and anyone can steer it with research directions. > **To suggest a research direction, comment on [Marin Belay Intake (#9514)](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9514).** Suggestions a maintainer approves (👍 from a `marin-devs` member) are copied into this thread automatically, and the agent acts only on this thread. This thread holds the agent's batch reports and maintainer steering. ![fast_track MoE ladder: Marin 535B baseline, clean KMA and candidate 9](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/marin-community/marin/9697c11ef215ec0f9d536a1bceb0876f768fcf26/v1/ladder_scaling.png) The Marin 535B compute-optimal baseline follows `L(C) = 1.2 + 59.0·C^(−0.0843)` over four data-matched rungs. Clean KMA, the current baseline (★), is 0.022 lower at d512, 0.049 lower at d768, 0.040 lower at d1024 and 0.033 lower at d1280, which is about 1.14×, 1.43×, 1.40× and 1.35× the baseline's compute efficiency. Its dashed curve is fit to all four points: `L(C) = 1.2 + 64.8·C^(−0.0870)`. The **?** marks the open question this issue is chasing: how much further down each point can go. The red diamonds are the current best recipe, candidate 9 (Status below): **2.977 / 2.725 / 2.515 / 2.397** at d512 / d768 / d1024 / d1280. d512 and d768 are seed means, and the bigram table follows rule A. d768–d1280 are data-matched; d512 sits at its fixed-time step count (2817 vs 2383 steps), so it's plotted slightly to the right. That is 0.157 / 0.098 / 0.078 / 0.074 below clean KMA. Its dash-dot curve is fit to all four points: `L(C) = 1.2 + 55.0·C^(−0.0847)`. Its slope is a little shallower than clean KMA's, so the gap narrows with compute: projected to **1e24 FLOPs, 1.710 vs clean KMA's 1.727, about 1.48× clean KMA's compute efficiency and 2.95× the 535B baseline's**. Because the fixed-time d512 point flattens the fitted slope, that projection is probably conservative. The right panel is clean KMA's training MFU at each rung on one 8×H100 node: 9.5% at d512 and d768, 12.2% at d1024, and 13.0% at d1280. FLOPs are counted from KMA's own layers (KDA, MLA + Inkling, AttnRes), as 3× forward with no recompute. The trainer's logged `throughput/mfu` uses the baseline architecture's FLOP formula, so it is slightly off for KMA. ## Objective **Minimize Paloma macro loss (`eval/paloma/macro_loss`, final step) at the d512 rung after a fixed 8 minutes of 8×H100 train-step time.** - **Fixed time, not fixed tokens.** Faster code trains on more tokens within the 8 minutes, so a pure speedup counts as a win. - The LR schedule depends on the step count, so fix steps before each run: `num_steps = round(480 s × ex/s ÷ batch)`. - Measure ex/s with a short `--no-eval` probe (~30 steps) on the same cluster, and use the steady-state throughput. - Compile, evals and startup are excluded from the 8 minutes. - **Numerics changes are allowed** (e.g. FP8, precision changes, approximate kernels). They count as ordinary wins; no parity check needed. - **Noise.** Differences under ~0.005 are noise. A win must beat the current best by more than 0.005. ### Gates (both relative to the current baseline, same fixed-time rule at each rung) - **Gate 1:** beat the baseline at d512 and d768. - **Gate 2:** also beat it at d1024 and d1280, **and** project to lower Paloma macro loss at 1e24 FLOPs. Fit a power law of final loss against training FLOPs across the four rungs, for both the baseline and the variant, fixing the asymptote to 1.2. ### Fixed - Training data, the 16k BPE tokenizer, and the eval sets. - Sequence length 4096. - One 8×H100 node per rung. - The FLOP accounting used for the gate-2 projection. ### Judgment calls - **Hero-scale speed is out of scope for v1, so use discretion.** - Robust target criteria would also check training speed and inference speed at hero scale. Marin Belay v1 skips those checks. - Judge whether a change's d512 gain would carry over to hero scale, and avoid changes whose gain comes from d512-only effects. Two examples: - Dropping MoE for dense would be a clear win at d512 because dense gets ~5× higher MFU there, but that MFU gain would not carry over at hero scale. - A much larger KV cache would also be a clear win at d512, but it would hurt long-context inference speed. - **Avoid magic numbers.** - Prefer changes with few new tuned constants. A tuned constant is justified when its gain is above the noise threshold and holds as a pattern across scales. For example, a 2× LR on one parameter group qualifies if it clears the noise threshold and the gain shows up consistently at larger rungs. - The higher a change's risk of curve fitting, the more scales it must be validated at before it counts as a win. - **Spend effort in proportion to an idea's likelihood of improvement.** - Promising ideas deserve several attempts. Long shots can be tried once and dropped. - A first run is not a verdict for a large change. If you try a new architecture or component, tune its optimizer assignment, LR, init and other key hyperparameters before concluding it doesn't work. The baseline's settings were tuned for the baseline, not for the new idea. ## Architecture (current best, d512) The diagrams below show **clean KMA**. The current best recipe adds the components listed under **Status → Current best recipe**: MLA key norm and key offset, a gated bigram-memory AttnRes source, ReLU² experts, and optimizer, schedule and logit changes. The diagrams show d512; the other rungs differ in the Shape table only. **1. Layer stack and Block Attention Residuals.** Every sublayer reads its input through its own AttnRes gate, a per-token softmax over the residual history. At d512 each layer closes an AttnRes block, so the history at layer *i* is the embedding plus one sum per earlier layer. [¹](#arch-note) ```mermaid flowchart TB tok["token ids

16384 × 512"] emb --> en["RMSNorm → GatedNorm"] en --> S0(["source 0

"block sum b0" .-> H L1 -. "b1" .-> H L2 -. "b2" .-> H L3 -. "b3" .-> H L4 -. "b4" .-> H S0 -.-> H H[("AttnRes history, read by every gate

fused CE, vocab tile 8192, z-loss 1e-4"] head --> loss(["next-token loss"]) ``` **2. One layer.** The two sublayers each have an AttnRes gate. The MoE gate also sees the attention output written just before it, as the running partial. ```mermaid flowchart TB Hin[("history

KDA (local) or MLA + Inkling (global)"}} MIX --> SCA["ShortConv (MLA layers only)"] --> PA(["partial = attn out"]) PA --> GM["AttnRes gate
history + partial"] Hin --> GM GM --> M1["RMSNorm → GatedNorm"] --> MOE{{"LatentMoE + 2 shared experts"}} MOE --> SCM["ShortConv"] --> PB(["block b_i = attn out + MoE out"]) PB --> Hout[("appended to history")] ``` **3a. Kimi Delta Attention, the local mixer (layers 0, 1, 2, 4 at d512; D = 512, 4 heads × 128).** ```mermaid flowchart TB kx["x"] --> kq["q = SiLU(ShortConv(x W_q))"] & kk["k = SiLU(ShortConv(x W_k))"] & kv["v = SiLU(ShortConv(x W_v))"] kx --> kg["decay g = −5 · σ(exp(A_log) · (x W_a↓ W_a↑ + dt_bias))
rank-128 gate, per channel; A_log per head"] kx --> kb["write strength β = σ(x W_β), per head"] kq & kk --> kn["L2-norm q, k; q × 1/√128"] kn & kv & kg & kb --> rec["delta rule, chunked Pallas kernels (chunk 16)
S_t = (I − β k kᵀ) Diag(e^g) S_{t−1} + β k vᵀ
o_t = S_tᵀ q_t · state resets at document starts"] rec --> kon["per-head RMSNorm (shared 128-wide scale)"] --> kog["× σ(x W_g), per channel"] --> ko["W_o → sublayer out
no RoPE, no window, no output ShortConv"] ``` **3b. MLA + Inkling, the global mixer (layers 3 and 5 at d512).** ```mermaid flowchart TB mx["x"] --> mq["q = x W_q (full rank, 4 × 128)"] mx --> ml["KV latent = RMSNorm(x W_dkv), 512 wide, learnable gain"] --> mk["k = latent W_uk"] & mv["v = latent W_uv"] mx --> rel["Inkling bias[h,i,j] = R[i,h,:] · P[:, i−j]
R = x W_r (16 per head) · P 16 × 1024, shared across heads"] mq & mk & mv & rel --> fa["FA4 causal attention (fwd + SM90 bwd)
logits × 1/√128 (qk_mult 1) · no RoPE · no QK-norm
Inkling bias added before softmax"] fa --> xsa["XSA: subtract each head's component along its own v"] --> mg["× 2σ(x W_gate), per head, zero-init"] --> mo["W_o → ShortConv → sublayer out"] ``` **3c. LatentMoE with quantile-balanced routing (every layer).** ```mermaid flowchart TB ex["x (512)"] --> fused["one fused GEMM:
router · W_latent↓ · shared-expert gate/up"] fused --> rt["router logits (fp32)
top-(8+1) on logit − β_QB; 9th = threshold α"] rt --> qb["QB: β_e = global (1 − 8/384) quantile of logit − α
10k-bin histogram each step; router bias = −β, not trained"] rt --> cw["combine weights = σ(unbiased logits) of the top 8,
renormalized to sum to 2.5"] fused --> lat["latent = RMSNorm(x W_latent↓), 256 wide"] lat & cw --> ep["384 SwiGLU experts, hidden 256
pooled-wave EP all-to-all over 8 GPUs, capacity 1.15"] ep --> up["W_latent↑ 256 → 512"] fused --> sh["2 shared SwiGLU experts, 512 → 256 → 512
down projections fused into one GEMM"] up & sh --> sum["routed + shared → ShortConv → sublayer out"] ``` ¹ AttnRes rolls a new block at layer *i* while `i % max(1, L // 8) == 0` and fewer than 8 blocks exist. At d512 and d768 every layer closes a block. At d1024 (12 layers) and d1280 (14 layers) only layers 0–7 do, so layers 8 and up all accumulate into one running partial instead of their own blocks. **Optimizer routing:** - **MuonH:** every attention and MoE matrix, and every GatedNorm (KDA `W_β` at 2× the MuonH LR). - **AdamH:** lm_head. - **Adam:** embedding, router, attention output gate, norm gains, ShortConv kernels, KDA decay parameters, Inkling weights. - **Adam at 0.1× the Adam LR:** the AttnRes queries. ## Baseline: clean KMA Branch [`fasttrack-moe-kma`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/fasttrack-moe-kma) @ `4eba59cafa`. Build from this branch. The recipe below covers every model and optimizer component. Values are for d512 unless noted; the code is `experiments/grug/fast_track/{model,optimizer,heuristic,launch}.py`. **Shape** | Rung | Width D | Layers | Local (KDA) / global (MLA) layers | Heads × head dim | Batch | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | d512 | 512 | 6 | 4 / 2 | 4 × 128 | 128 | | d768 | 768 | 8 | 6 / 2 | 6 × 128 | 128 | | d1024 | 1024 | 12 | 9 / 3 | 8 × 128 | 256 | | d1280 | 1280 | 14 | 10 / 4 | 10 × 128 | 256 | - Every 4th layer and the last layer are global; all other layers are local. - The run uses a 16k vocab and sequence length 4096 with packed documents. Every ShortConv and the KDA state respect document boundaries (the KDA state resets at each document start). - Weights are initialized with std 0.5/√D. Compute is bf16. **Embedding and output** - Token embedding → RMSNorm → GatedNorm. The result is AttnRes source 0. - Output path: final AttnRes gate → RMSNorm → GatedNorm → untied lm_head (`output_proj`). - The fused lm_head + cross-entropy loop uses a vocab tile of 8192. - GatedNorm (every GatedNorm in the model) is `x · sigmoid(W_up · SiLU(W_down · x))`, with a rank-128 bottleneck. **Block (every layer)** - **Attention sublayer:** input = its AttnRes gate mix → RMSNorm → GatedNorm → mixer (KDA or MLA). - **MoE sublayer:** input = its AttnRes gate mix → RMSNorm → GatedNorm → MoE → ShortConv on the MoE output. - Each ShortConv is a 4-tap causal depthwise conv. **Local layers: Kimi Delta Attention** (Kimi K3's layer) - **Projections:** q/k/v are D → N·128 with full heads (no GQA). Each goes through a ShortConv followed by SiLU. q and k are L2-normalized, and q is scaled by 1/√128. - **Decay:** per-channel log-decay `g = −5·sigmoid(exp(A_log)·(x·W_a_down·W_a_up + dt_bias))`. - The gate projection has rank 128. - `A_log` is one value per head, initialized to 0. - `dt_bias` is one value per channel, initialized so the decay rate spans 0.02–0.5. - **Write strength:** `β = sigmoid(x·W_β)`, one value per head. - **Recurrence:** `S_t = (I − β·k·kᵀ)·Diag(exp(g))·S_{t−1} + β·k·vᵀ`, read out as `o_t = S_tᵀ·q_t`. - It runs as chunked Pallas kernels, with a stable block-doubling inverse inside each chunk. - **Output:** per-head RMSNorm with a learnable 128-wide scale shared across heads → full-rank per-channel gate `sigmoid(x·W_g)` → `W_o`. - No positional encoding, no window, no XSA, and no ShortConv on the branch output. **Global layers: MLA + Inkling relative position** - **q:** full-rank, D → N·128 (no Q latent). - **k and v:** k = `W_uk · RMSNorm(x·W_dkv)` and v = `W_uv · RMSNorm(x·W_dkv)`. - They share one 512-wide KV latent, with a learnable RMSNorm on the latent. - Heads are 128 wide with no RoPE part. - There's no ShortConv on K, so the up-projections can be absorbed at inference. - **Scaling:** no QK-norm; `qk_mult` = 1, i.e. standard 1/√128 logit scaling. - **Position — Inkling relative-position bias**, added to the pre-softmax logits in place of RoPE: - `bias[h,i,j] = R[i,h,:] · P[:, i−j]`, where `R = x·W_r` is 16 values per head. - `P` is a bank of shape [16 × 1024] shared across heads. The relative extent is 1024. - It runs inside the FA4 attention kernel (forward, backward, and the SM90 backward pass). - **XSA** (exclusive self-attention): subtract the component of each head's output that is parallel to its own value vector. - **Output gate:** per head, `2·sigmoid(x·W_gate)`. `W_gate` is zero-initialized, so the gate is 1 at init. - The branch output also gets a ShortConv. **MoE sublayer (LatentMoE with quantile-balanced routing)** - **Experts:** 384 routed experts, top-8. Each is a SwiGLU with hidden size D/2. - **Latent space:** experts operate in a D/2-wide latent. The input goes through `W_latent_down` → RMSNorm, and the combined expert output goes back up through `W_latent_up`. - **Router:** reads the full-width token and computes logits in fp32. - Experts are selected by top-(8+1) on bias-adjusted logits, where the 9th logit is the threshold α. - Combine weights are the sigmoid of the unbiased logits, renormalized to sum to 2.5. - **Quantile balancing:** each step, each expert's threshold β is the global (1 − K/E) quantile of the logit margins (logit − α), read from a 10k-bin histogram. The router bias is set to −β. - The router bias is not trained by gradient. - **Capacity:** capacity factor 1.15, with pooled-wave expert-parallel dispatch. Receiver ranks are sort-based and the expand backward is gather-based. - **Shared experts:** 2 shared SwiGLU experts that bypass the latent: D → D/2 hidden → D. - **Fused projections:** - The router, latent-down, and both shared experts' gate/up projections run as one GEMM. - The shared experts' down-projections run as one GEMM. **Residual stream: Block Attention Residuals** - **Sources:** the embedding source, one running sum per completed block of sublayer outputs, and the running partial sum of the current block. - The model has 8 blocks. Block sums use the raw sublayer outputs. - **Gates:** every sublayer (attention and MoE) has its own gate, and there is one final gate before the output norm. Each gate has one learned pseudo-query `q ∈ ℝᴰ`, zero-initialized so every gate starts as a uniform average. - **Mixing:** per token, `logitᵢ = q · rms_norm(sourceᵢ)`, using a parameter-free (frozen) RMS key norm, then `softmax` over sources and a weighted sum of the raw sources. - **Implementation:** - Each completed block is scored once against every gate that reads it. - Backward: at d512 the layer's forward intermediates are saved. At d768–d1280 each layer is recomputed. At d1280 the attention branch is also rematerialized. - The model keeps one layer stack per mixer kind. **Optimizer** | Group | Update rule | LR | Parameters | |---|---|---|---| | `muonh` | MuonH | MuonH LR | all attention and MoE matrices: MLA `W_q`/`W_dkv`/`W_uk`/`W_uv`/`W_o`; KDA `W_q`/`W_k`/`W_v`/`W_o`/`W_g`; experts; shared experts; latent down/up. Also every GatedNorm `W_down`/`W_up`. | | `kda_beta` | MuonH | 2 × MuonH LR | KDA `W_β` | | `adamh` | AdamH | MuonH LR | lm_head (`output_proj`) | | `adam` | Adam | Adam LR | token embedding; router; attention output gate; router bias slot (overwritten by QB); all 1-D norm gains; ShortConv kernels; KDA `W_a_down`/`W_a_up`, `A_log`, `dt_bias`; Inkling `W_r` and `P` | | `attn_res_query` | Adam | 0.1 × Adam LR | the AttnRes pseudo-queries | - **MuonH:** Nesterov momentum 0.95 → Newton–Schulz orthogonalization (5 quintic steps, bucketed across same-shape matrices) → a step along that direction, then projection back onto the matrix's Frobenius sphere. Each matrix's norm stays fixed at its init value. - **AdamH:** the Adam direction with the same Frobenius-sphere (hyperball) projection. - **Adam:** β1 0.9. Only the router and the attention output gate get decoupled weight decay (0.02). No other parameter gets weight decay, and there's no gradient clipping. - **Schedule:** 1% warmup, then linear decay to 0.05× peak. - **Peak values** from `MoeHeuristic` (they depend on tokens, width and batch): - Adam LR = `0.0876 · tokens^−0.346 · D^−0.345 · √(tokens per batch)`. - MuonH LR = 13/3 × Adam LR. - β2 = `0.999^(tokens per batch / 131072)`. - ε = `9.68e−18 · √(steps)`. - At d512 with 2384 steps: MuonH LR 0.0227, Adam LR 0.0052, β2 0.996, ε 4.7e−16. Submit (the default priority is interactive): ``` NO_PROXY="*" uv run python -m experiments.grug.fast_track.launch --submit \ --target-cluster cw-us-east-02a --priority interactive \ --run-id --size d512 --recipe kma --num-steps <8-min steps> --version ``` ## Compute - cw-us-east-02a at **interactive** priority. - **At most 10 active runs at once**, probes included. - **Limit runs above d768** to keep the experimentation rate high. d1024 and d1280 runs take hours and hold a slot the whole time, so save them for changes that have already passed gate 1 or that need extra scales because of curve-fitting risk. - Don't save checkpoints (the launcher default). ## For humans Comment with a research direction for the agent, for example "try X", or "combine A and B". The agent picks up new comments at its next batch. The main goal of a single experiment should be to learn about the system. This means that if you tweak one knob and the loss goes off the rails, the experiment can still be considered a success! We better understand the system sensitivity! Building knowledge through failed experiments will bring us closer to the long term goal of better models. ## For the agent - Read `experiments/grug/fast_track/README.md` and `agent.md` first. Where they differ from this issue, this issue wins; the main difference is the fixed-time objective. - Run 5–10 experiments per batch, and prioritize human comments when picking the next one. - Ask for clarification in the thread if helpful, but never hold a batch waiting for an answer: state your assumption and correct it in the next batch. - Start at d512. When a change beats the current best by more than 0.005, validate it at d768. - Post **one comment per batch** and edit it as runs finish. Start it with 🤖 and include: - the batch goal, and which human comments it addresses; - a table with one row per run: change | branch@commit | W&B link | steps | ex/s | mid loss | final Paloma macro loss | Δ vs current best; - a 1–3 line takeaway and the planned next batch. - **Branches:** prefix with `ladderclimb_v1_`, and link the exact commit each job ran. - **W&B:** project `marin_moe`, with short prefixed run IDs such as `lc1-b03-…` (names over 128 characters fail at init). - Add the `agent-generated` label to any issue or PR you open. - Keep the **Status** table below updated with a concise chronology of improvements. ## Studies Deep dives and multi-batch studies, newest first. comments.body:
Some ideas to get started. Treat this as a general pool of ideas, that indicates the spirit of what can be tried.
1. https://blog.tilderesearch.com/blog/online-kl-shampoo. Consider interactions with hyperball and selectively replace matrices.
2. Add a second embedding table with its own random init. Attn residuals queries both embedding tables, treating them as unique inputs.
3. Lets add value embeddings. That is, a second embedding table that gets added to V on the MLA layers. So take KV latent-> project to num_heads of size 128. Then do values = lambda1*values + lambda2*value_embeds[layer_i]. lambda 1 init to 1, lambda2 init to 0. value_embeds has [vocab_size, num_heads*head_dim, num_mla_layers] dimension. Can also try gated value embeds, where instead of lambda2, its conditional on residual stream via sigmoid(linear(x)).
4. Add learnable scalars to each submodule output, that feeds into attention residuals. May be worth tracking and plotting these in wandb, to see if indicates any architecture changes will help.
5. Try different variations of linear attention to replace KDA.
6. It has been shown in many places that the final couple layers of attention dont prefer to attend to outputs from the final MLPs. See if there is any change to attention residuals to help make this more natural.
7. Adding an lm_head auxillary loss to the output of layer 1 for the first X (say 500) steps can help give the routed experts a cleaner role early. Unclear how this interacts with attention residuals.
8. Hash routing on first layer.
9. Instead of Adam/AdamH on embed and lm_head, look into other optimizers here that have shown promise in literature.
10. Do any weights benefit from extremely different beta1/beta2/momentum terms, or swapping their optimizer group.
11. Update the router behavior (sigmoid vs softmax), normalizing over picked experts vs not, sampling over experts instead of top k).
12. Null routing (enable tokens to select null experts which skips their computation, dynamic compute per token).
13. Multi-token-prediction.
14. Sparse attention.

If users give comments with singular specific ideas, give it priority over this laundry list.

🤖 **Batch 1: cheap architecture adds from the idea list, an LR check, and a noise and profile baseline** (d512, 2475 steps) — **done**

**Goal.** Test the lowest-cost ideas from @ClassicLarry's list: `#2` (second embedding table), `#3` (value embeddings, both forms), and `#4` (learnable sublayer output scalars, logged to W&B). Also check whether the `MoeHeuristic` LR, which was fit on the old baseline architecture, is still right for KMA (×1.5 and ×0.67 on both LRs). Add a seed-1 baseline to calibrate noise, and a 60-step profile to find speed levers. Speed counts as a win under the fixed-time objective.

**Assumption (I'll correct it next batch if it's wrong).** None of these changes adds meaningful compute, so all runs use the baseline's 2475 steps instead of a separate probe. After each run I check its steady-state ex/s. If it is more than about 1% below 660, I rerun at `round(480 × ex/s / 128)` steps. Branch [`ladderclimb_v1_batch01`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/eb26f3cbc9) @ `eb26f3cbc9`: every change is gated by a `--model-set` / `--opt-set` flag and defaults to off.

**Implementation details**
- **ve:** each MLA layer gets a [16384 × N·128] table, and `v = λ1·v + λ2·VE[token]` (λ1 = 1, λ2 = 0 at init). The tables, λ and the gate go to Adam at the Adam LR, like `token_embed`.
- **veg:** `v = λ1·v + sigmoid(x·W)·VE[token]`, with one gate per head. `W` is zero-initialized, so the gate starts at 0.5.
- **osc:** a scalar initialized to 1 on each attention and MoE sublayer output before it enters the AttnRes history (Adam). Logged as `train/attn_res/scale_{attn,mlp}_L*`.
- **emb2:** a second randomly initialized table → learnable RMSNorm, prepended as an extra AttnRes block that every gate can read.

**Takeaway.**
- **Noise is the story.** The identical-code seed-1 baseline landed at 3.1195, 0.0056 below seed 0. Against the two-seed baseline mean of 3.1223, none of the architecture changes clears noise: emb2 −0.005, veg −0.004, osc −0.002, ve −0.002. ve, veg and emb2 also ran 7–13% slower, so at a fair 8-minute step count they would lose part of that.
- **The LR heuristic holds for KMA.** Both ×1.5 and ×0.67 are clearly worse.
- **The learned scalars in osc point at the MoE output.** Its final values: MoE outputs grow to 1.2 / 1.4 / 1.5 / 2.1 / 1.7 / 1.9× by layer, the early KDA outputs shrink to 0.48×, and the MLA outputs stay near 1.0. The routed-expert output magnitude is capped by MuonH's sphere and the 2.5 combine renorm, and it wants to grow.
- **Profile (8×H100, d512, ~187 ms/step).** Compute is ~155 ms: elementwise fusions ~61, GEMMs ~43, sort/scatter/gather ~23, KDA ~14, FA4 ~7. Exposed EP all-to-all is ~18 ms, and the host gap between steps is ~6 ms.
  - **One kernel is a bug:** the token-embedding gradient takes **~11 ms/step**. Under the bf16 compute policy, the gather's transpose scatter-adds every token's cotangent directly into a **bf16** table. That means contended bf16 atomics, with frequent tokens' gradients rounded at every add. A single-GPU microbenchmark puts the fp32 scatter at 0.2 ms. The same scatter is why ve, veg and emb2 were slow: each extra table adds one.

**Next (batch 2).**
- Fix the embedding backward with an fp32 scatter-add plus a psum: [`ladderclimb_v1_batch02` @ `269387e86b`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/269387e86b). It is a pure speed and precision change, so it is a baseline candidate in its own right.
- Probe throughput with the fix, then rerun ve, veg and emb2 on it at fair step counts, with replicate seeds.
- Test MoE output-magnitude variants: combine renorm sum 2.5 → 4, sigmoid without renorm, softmax combine, and K3's normalized LatentMoE.
- In response to the literature-scan comment: a background scan turned up these candidates for later batches: K3 normalized LatentMoE, per-head Muon, NorMuon-style row normalization, Engram n-gram memory, null experts, and FP8 lm_head.
**Next batch (tentative):** act on the profile. Validate any win above 0.005 at d768. Try combinations of the winners, MTP, and router variants (`#11`).

🤖 **Batch 5: @ClassicLarry's three requests: z-loss weight, projection biases, and freezing QB at 50%** (d512, 2817 steps; reference = batch-3 base mean **3.0990**)

**Addresses** the comment asking to vary the logit z-loss, add biases to some weight matrices, and freeze QB updates halfway through training. All runs build on the fp32-embedding base, branch [`ladderclimb_v1_batch05`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/ea0592bd02).
- **z-loss:** the current weight is 1e-4 (`--z-loss-weight`). One run turns it off, one raises it 10×.
- **Biases:** zero-initialized and trained with Adam, at three sites:
  - Qwen-style q/k/v: KDA q/k/v before their ShortConvs, and MLA q plus the KV latent before its RMSNorm.
  - The attention sublayer output.
  - The MoE sublayer output.

  If the combined run moves, I'll split the sites next batch.
- **QB freeze:** from step 1408 on, the router bias keeps its last quantile-balanced value (`qb_freeze_step`). Routing can then drift, and load balance is no longer enforced.

| biases: q/k/v + attention out + MoE out | [`ea0592bd02`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/ea0592bd02) | [lc1-b05-bias](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc1-b05-bias) | 2817 | 742 (−1%) | 3.3913 | 3.0993 | +0.0003 |
| freeze QB router biases at step 1408 (50%) | [`ea0592bd02`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/ea0592bd02) | [lc1-b05-qbfrz](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc1-b05-qbfrz) | 2817 | 751 | 3.3924 | 3.1059 | +0.0069 |
| **AttnRes logit bias** per (gate, source), zero-init, Adam at 0.1× (human, 2nd comment) | [`f1734ddcdf`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/f1734ddcdf) | [lc1-b05-arb](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc1-b05-arb) | 2817 | 751 | 3.3954 | 3.1001 | +0.0011 |
| AttnRes logit bias + AttnRes z-loss 1e-3 | [`f1734ddcdf`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/f1734ddcdf) | [lc1-b05-arbz3](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc1-b05-arbz3) | 2817 | 748 | 3.3996 | 3.1045 | +0.0055 |
| AttnRes logit bias + AttnRes z-loss 1e-1 | [`f1734ddcdf`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/f1734ddcdf) | [lc1-b05-arbz1](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc1-b05-arbz1) | 2817 | 746 | 3.4570 | 3.1475 | +0.0485 |

**AttnRes logit bias and z-loss** (added for the follow-up comment). Each of the 13 gates gets a zero-init bias per source it reads: one per completed block, plus one for the running partial. It is added to the logit before the softmax and trained with Adam at 0.1× the Adam LR, the same as the queries. The z-loss is the mean over tokens of logsumexp(gate logits)², averaged over gates, and added to the loss. Every run now logs the pseudo-query norms: `train/attn_res/query_norm_{mean,max,gNN}` plus the unweighted `train/attn_res/z`. One caveat: a z-loss can be satisfied by shifting a gate's biases down together, which leaves the mix unchanged. I'll compare the q norms across the three runs.

**Correction:** the AttnRes z-loss runs' eval losses also included the z-loss term (the same bug, found in batch 18). That inflated them by weight × z: about +0.0012 for 1e-3 and +0.001 for 1e-1. Their deltas are about +0.004 and +0.047 instead of +0.0055 and +0.0485, so both are still worse.

**Takeaway (all done).**
- **AttnRes logit bias is neutral (+0.0011).**
- **The AttnRes z-loss hurts:** +0.0055 at 1e-3 and +0.049 at 1e-1.
- **It raises the pseudo-query norms rather than lowering them.** Final values:

  | run | AttnRes z (unweighted) | query norm mean | query norm max |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | bias only | 6.31 | 0.227 | 0.377 |
  | bias + z 1e-3 | 1.23 | 0.286 | 0.583 |
  | bias + z 1e-1 | 0.01 | 0.332 | 0.565 |

  The z-loss is minimized by pushing every logit down. With keys that are RMS-normalized but not mean-centred, the query does this by growing along the direction opposite the common component of the sources, instead of shifting all biases together. That distorts the mix.
- The other results from this batch:
  - Freezing QB at 50%: +0.007.
  - lm_head z-loss 1e-3: +0.006.
  - lm_head z-loss 0: −0.002.
  - Projection biases: neutral.

comments.author: ClassicLarry
comments.body:
🤖 **Batch 9: looped models (@neel04's request): tied looping, with and without growth, with input injection** (d512, paired seed 0 vs qk_mult-2.5 base **3.0858**)

**Addresses** @neel04's comment. It follows [slowrun#92](https://github.com/qlabs-eng/slowrun/pull/92) (1× for 70% of training, then 2×) and [arXiv 2609.19107](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.19107) (boundary operator `Norm(h) + α·e`, growth partway through training, backprop through all passes, and FLOPs of every pass counted). Branch [`ladderclimb_v1_batch09`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/c2803601b0).

**How it maps onto KMA** (`loop_passes`, `loop_grow_step`):
- **The looped core is the whole 6-layer stack**, weights tied. Each pass extends the Block AttnRes history. Pass 2's gates read the embedding, every pass-1 block, and the pass-2 blocks so far. Pass 2 has its own zero-initialized AttnRes pseudo-queries, so its gates start as uniform averages over that longer history.
- **Input injection.** At the start of each extra pass, the running partial is initialized to `α·e`, where e is the normalized embedding source and α is learned (init 1, Adam), and the pass's layers write onto it. The AttnRes gates already see e as source 0. This is the explicit re-injection from both references. The AttnRes softmax already normalizes what each sublayer reads, which plays the part of `Norm(h)`.
- **Growth** uses a step-gated `lax.cond`. Before the growth step only pass 1 executes, at full base speed. After it both passes run, with gradients through both. The router biases are shared per physical layer; their QB statistics are averaged over the passes.
- **Fixed-time steps.** Two passes run at 0.506× the base throughput (80-step probe: 381.8 vs 754.1 ex/s), so every run is given 8 minutes of train-step time:
  - loop2 throughout: 1426 steps.
  - Grow at 70%: N solves `0.7N/751 + 0.3N/380 = 480/128`, so N = 2179 and growth is at step 1525.
  - Grow at 50%: N = 1892, growth at step 946.
- **Not in this batch: untied growth**, where the core is copied at the growth step and the copies train separately. It changes the parameter tree and optimizer state mid-run, so it needs trainer work. It's next if tied growth looks promising.

| change | branch@commit | W&B | steps | ex/s | mid loss | final Paloma macro loss | Δ (paired) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| loop ×2 throughout (tied, injection) | [`c2803601b0`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/c2803601b0) | [lc1-b09-loop2](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc1-b09-loop2) | 1426 | 381 | 3.5052 | 3.1766 | **+0.0908** |
| grow 1→2 passes at 70% of steps (step 1525) | [`c2803601b0`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/c2803601b0) | [lc1-b09-grow70](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc1-b09-grow70) | 2179 | | | OOM: 79.8 GiB (lax.cond kept both branches' buffers); fixed, rerun below | |
| grow 1→2 passes at 50% (step 946) | [`c2803601b0`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/c2803601b0) | [lc1-b09-grow50](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc1-b09-grow50) | 1892 | | | OOM: 79.8 GiB (lax.cond kept both branches' buffers); fixed, rerun below | |
| grow 1→2 at 70% (step 1525), static per-phase programs | [`0d023baad9`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/0d023baad9) | [lc1-b09-grow70b](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc1-b09-grow70b) | 2179 | 747 → 380 | 3.5435* | 3.1065 | +0.0207 |
| grow 1→2 at 50% (step 946), static per-phase programs | [`0d023baad9`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/0d023baad9) | [lc1-b09-grow50b](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc1-b09-grow50b) | 1892 | 747 → 380 | 3.5647* | 3.1195 | +0.0337 |

The mid-run eval always runs every pass, so for the growth runs the mid loss evaluates a model that has not trained its second pass yet. Only the final loss is comparable.

**Takeaway.**
- **Looping loses at d512 fixed time**, in every variant:

  | variant | Δ |
  |---|---|
  | 2× throughout | +0.091 |
  | grow 1→2 at 50% | +0.034 |
  | grow 1→2 at 70% | +0.021 |

  The less time spent in the 2× slower phase, the smaller the loss. The measured phase throughputs, 747 then 380 ex/s, match the budget, so all three got 8 minutes. \* marks mid losses from evals that ran both passes before the second pass had trained.
- **Why it loses.** The paper's gains are compute multipliers at ≥1e20 FLOPs with 7–8 tokens per parameter for its growth variants. Here the whole run is about 1e17 FLOPs and data-limited: in 8 minutes the model sees only about 1.1B tokens. An extra pass costs tokens, which are the scarce resource at this rung. Untied growth has the same FLOP cost after growth, so I'm not building it for d512. It is a better fit for a hero-scale study.

**Earlier notes.**
- **Fixed 2× looping throughout is much worse at fixed time: +0.091.** It gets only 1426 steps. At d512, one pass of the 6-layer stack is not the bottleneck; tokens seen are.
- **The growth runs first OOMed.** The step-gated `lax.cond` allocated 79.8 GiB, because XLA holds buffers for both branches. I replaced it with two statically compiled train steps, a one-pass program before the growth step and a two-pass one after, chosen per step in Python ([`0d023baad9`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/0d023baad9)). Its CPU check matches the plain model exactly.

comments.body: Let’s try slimming some things down. Drop the gated norm on embed, gated norm on lm head, and make the attn gate on kda just per head instead of per channel. Try these independently.

comments.author: ClassicLarry
comments.body:
🤖 **Batch 10: slimming ablations (@ClassicLarry's request)** (d512, 2817 steps, paired seed 0 vs the qk_mult-2.5 base **3.0858**)

**Addresses** the comment asking to drop the GatedNorm on the embedding, drop the GatedNorm on the lm_head input, and make the KDA output gate per head instead of per channel. Each runs independently on top of qk_mult 2.5. All three remove compute, so running them at the base's 2817 steps slightly under-credits them, which is the conservative direction.
- `embed_gated_norm=false`: embedding → RMSNorm only.
- `final_gated_norm=false`: final AttnRes gate → RMSNorm → lm_head.
- `kda_gate_per_head=true`: `W_g` becomes [D, N] instead of [D, N·128], and `σ(x W_g)` is broadcast over each head's 128 channels. It stays on MuonH, like `W_β`.

| change | branch@commit | W&B | steps | ex/s | mid loss | final Paloma macro loss | Δ (paired) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| no GatedNorm on the embedding | [`afa837be5f`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/afa837be5f) | [lc1-b10-noembgn](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc1-b10-noembgn) | 2817 | 748 | 3.3773 | 3.0863 | +0.0005 |
| no GatedNorm before the lm_head | [`afa837be5f`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/afa837be5f) | [lc1-b10-nofingn](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc1-b10-nofingn) | 2817 | 749 | 3.3822 | 3.0864 | +0.0006 |
| KDA output gate per head (not per channel) | [`afa837be5f`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/afa837be5f) | [lc1-b10-kdagh](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc1-b10-kdagh) | 2817 | 705 (−6%, see below) | 3.3877 | 3.0912 | **+0.0054** |
| both GatedNorms removed (embedding + lm_head input) | [`0d023baad9`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/0d023baad9) | [lc1-b10-nogn2](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc1-b10-nogn2) | 2817 | 752 | 3.3803 | **3.0821** | **−0.0037** |

**Takeaway.**
- **Both GatedNorm removals are neutral** (+0.0005 embedding, +0.0006 lm_head input), so they are free simplifications. **Removing both gives 3.0821 (−0.0037)**, so they stack. The model is simpler and, if anything, better. The batch-12 bundle drops both.
- **The per-head KDA output gate is worse: +0.0054 at the same 2817 steps.** The per-channel gate carries information. It also ran 6% slower, because my `jnp.repeat` broadcast of the gate didn't fuse; a reshape to `[B, S, N, 128]` would avoid that. The step count was the same as the base, so the loss comparison is fair either way. Not pursuing it.

comments.author: AMX07
comments.body:
try NoPE on the MLA layers (drop Inkling), following Kimi K3 [https://github.com/MoonshotAI/Kimi-K3/blob/main/k3_tech_report.pdf](url)

K3 and Kimi Linear both pair KDA with NoPE MLA, relying on KDA's recurrent decay for position. KMA already has the same pieces (KDA before every MLA layer, q/k/v ShortConvs), so Inkling may be redundant here.

From Opus 5.5:

**Implementation (small):**

- `GrugModelConfig.__post_init__`: remove the `mla requires inkling_relpos` check. MLA layers are all global, so `disable_rope=True` there, and removing `rel_pos` gives pure NoPE (no RoPE, no bias).
- `CausalSelfAttention.init`, MLA branch: `rel_pos=InklingRelPos.init(...) if cfg.inkling_relpos else None`.
- Check that the optimizer group routing Inkling `W_r`/`P` to Adam doesn't break when they're absent.

**Runs (d512, paired seed 0 vs the qk_mult-2.5 base, 3.0858):**
1. NoPE, qk_mult 2.5, steps from its own ex/s probe.
2. NoPE, qk_mult 2.0 and 3.5 (the current optimum was tuned with Inkling present).
3. Diagnostic: NoPE token-matched at 2817 steps, to separate "learns as well" from "trains faster."
4. If it loses slightly, try NoPE + ShortConv on MLA q only (keeps W_uk absorbable).

Replicate on seeds 1–2 if it clears 0.005 paired.

**For gate 2:** `attn_res_remat_attention` is forced on at d1280 partly because of the `[B, H, S, W]` Inkling bias. NoPE might let that remat be dropped at larger rungs, which is an extra speed gain there.

| NoPE + ShortConv on MLA q, qk_mult 2.5 | [`4b9b01f54b`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/4b9b01f54b) | [lc1-b11-nopeqc](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc1-b11-nopeqc) | 2880 | 767 | 3.3925 | 3.0880 | +0.0022 |
| NoPE + ShortConv on MLA q, qk_mult 3.0 | [`4b9b01f54b`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/4b9b01f54b) | [lc1-b11-nopeqc-qk30](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc1-b11-nopeqc-qk30) | 2880 | 766 | 3.3842 | 3.0876 | +0.0018 |
| Inkling (kept) + ShortConv on MLA q | [`4b9b01f54b`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/4b9b01f54b) | [lc1-b11-inkqc](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc1-b11-inkqc) | 2817 | 740 (−1.5%) | 3.3843 | 3.0881 | +0.0023 |

**Takeaway.**
- **NoPE MLA is roughly on par with Inkling at d512: +0.002 to +0.003, not better.**
  - qk_mult 2.5 and 3.5 score +0.0033 and +0.0026.
  - qk_mult 2.0 is clearly worse, at +0.0101.
  - So the qk_mult optimum found with Inkling holds without it.
- **The token-matched run separates the two effects.** At equal steps NoPE is **+0.009** worse, so Inkling helps learning by about 0.009 per step, and NoPE's +2.4% speed wins back about 0.006 of that.
- **ShortConv on MLA q** (K3's layout; W_uk stays absorbable) brings NoPE a bit closer (+0.0022 / +0.0018), but not past Inkling. On top of Inkling it does not help (+0.0023) and costs 1.5% throughput.
- **Verdict:** keep Inkling. Same-seed reruns differ by about 0.002, so this whole batch sits within about one noise unit of the base. NoPE is still worth a look at d1280, where dropping the `[B, H, S, W]` bias could remove the forced attention remat and speed that rung up. I'll check it when gate 2 is underway.

🤖 **Batch 13: tune on top of the bundle** (d512, 2817 steps, paired seed 0 vs the batch-12 bundle's seed 0 = **3.0836**)

**Goal.** Cheap checks that the bundle's settings haven't moved the optima, plus two speed levers. All runs use the full bundle flags.

comments.body:
🤖 **Batch 14: AttnRes source-weight plot, low-rank KDA β MLP, smaller MLA KV (@ClassicLarry's requests)** (d512, 2817 steps, paired seed 0 vs the current best config's seed 0: qk 2.5 + β1 0.8 + z-loss 0 = **3.0805**)

**Addresses** the comment asking for (1) an average AttnRes distribution plot, (2) a low-rank MLP for KDA β with tuned init, LR and optimizer, and (3) smaller or reused KV. Branch [`ladderclimb_v1_batch14` @ `eb17304a56`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/eb17304a56).

1. **AttnRes weight logging.** Every gate now logs its token-mean softmax weight per source, as `train/attn_res/w_gNN_bMM` (source = block MM) and `w_gNN_p` (the running partial). At d512, block 00 is the embedding and block k is layer k−1's output. Gates are numbered attn₀, MoE₀, …, attn₅, MoE₅, final. `lc1-b14-ref` reruns the current best config with this logging. I'll post a gates × sources heatmap at a few training steps once it finishes.
2. **KDA β MLP:** `β = σ(SiLU(x W_β↓) W_β↑)`, rank 16 (`kda_beta_rank`). Variants:
   - MuonH at 2× (the current `W_β` group) with random init.
   - Adam with random init.
   - Adam with `W_β↑` zero-initialized, so β = 0.5 at start like LoRA. Zero init can't use MuonH, which keeps each matrix at its initial norm.
   - An LR check if one wins.
3. **Smaller KV.** The MLA KV latent is the only KV cache that grows with context; KDA's state is fixed-size. I'm trying latent 256 and 128 (currently 512). Cross-layer latent reuse, with layer 5 reading layer 3's latent, comes next if the smaller latents hold up.

The launcher bundles the working tree. Three runs were submitted a moment before the commit landed, and ran with the same code as `eb17304a56` (the only difference is a docstring). The submit script now refuses a dirty tree.

![AttnRes source weights](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/marin-community/marin/75caa89903ede30815f61c23ef54ca935ec43141/v1/attnres_weights_lc1-b14-ref.png)

What the average distribution shows (final step):
- **Attention gates mostly read the immediately preceding layer's output**, a learned residual stream. The weight on it decays with depth: L1 0.73, L2 0.66, L3 0.48, L4 0.43.
- **The last MLA layer (L5) is the exception.** It puts 0.32 on L2's output, more than on L3 (0.17) or L4 (0.15), so it skips back over the two most recent layers. That fits idea `#6` (late attention layers don't want the latest sublayer outputs).
- **MoE gates mostly read their own layer's attention output (the partial):** 0.85 at L0, down to 0.40 at L4. L5's MoE instead splits across L3 out (0.18), L4 out (0.31) and the partial (0.31).
- **The final gate feeding the lm_head uses almost only the last three layers:** L3 0.16, L4 0.33, L5 0.41. The embedding and L0–L2 get ≤ 0.05 there, although every attention gate keeps 0.13–0.27 on the embedding.
- **The pattern forms early.** By step 1408 it is nearly final, and at step 100 the gates are still close to uniform.

Also: the rerun of the current best config landed at 3.0788 vs 3.0805 before, on the same seed. **Same-seed reruns differ by about 0.002** from GPU nondeterminism, so paired Δ below about 0.003 is noise.

**Takeaway.**
- **KDA β as a rank-16 MLP is neutral in every variant:** −0.0004 (MuonH 2×, random init), +0.0006 (Adam), +0.0012 (Adam with W_β↑ zero-init). The linear β already seems to capture what the gate needs at this scale. Two more tunings follow in batch 15: rank 64 and a higher Adam LR.
- **A smaller MLA KV latent clearly hurts:** 512 → 256 gives +0.016 and → 128 gives +0.019, with no measurable speedup at d512. Attention there is a small share of step time. Batch 15 tests cross-layer reuse instead: the last MLA layer reads the first MLA layer's KV latent, which halves the MLA cache.

Lets do full attention residuals, not block, so we can see if there are clear trends in attending to priror MLP or prior ATTN outputs. Also, plot how the grad norm changes by layer for the routed experts, shared experts, and attn parameters. want to see if layer zero routed experts are dying.

comments.author: ClassicLarry
comments.body:
🤖 **Batch 15: full AttnRes, per-layer gradient norms, per-expert hyperball (@ClassicLarry), plus KV reuse and β-MLP tuning** (d512, 2817 steps, paired seed 0 vs the current best config, qk 2.5 + β1 0.8 + z-loss 0: **3.0797**, the mean of two same-seed runs)

**Addresses** the comment asking for full AttnRes to see MLP-vs-attention source trends, per-layer gradient norms for routed experts, shared experts and attention (are layer-0 routed experts dying?), and a hyperball per expert. Also continues batch 14's KV-reuse and β-MLP requests. Branch [`ladderclimb_v1_batch14` @ `7112828d18`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/7112828d18).

**Per-layer gradient norms** ([lc1-b14-ref](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc1-b14-ref), current best config; W&B already logs these per layer; 25-point rolling median, log scale):

![per-layer gradient norms](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/marin-community/marin/55097ad3a9b3d66a0edffc0d066535971cc669d3/v1/gradnorm_lc1-b14-ref.png)

- **Layer-0 routed experts are not dying.** Their gradient norm *rises* over training, from 0.015 early to 0.019 at the end. That is on par with L1 (0.018) and above L2 (0.016). Every layer's routed-expert gradient norm grows across training, the global layers L3–L5 most (0.024–0.027).
- **The shared experts do the opposite.** Their gradient norms fall after about step 1300 in every layer; L0 drops from 0.021 to 0.011. The shared path does its learning early, and the routed experts carry the later learning.
- **Attention gradients decay steadily** from their early peak, fastest in L0. The exception is L5 (last MLA): it dips early and then climbs back to the second-largest norm.
- A layer-mean norm can hide individual dead experts. The per-expert routing counts are computed but not logged. If you want per-expert detail, I'll add a per-expert load / grad-norm histogram next.

**Runs**
- **Full AttnRes** (`attn_res_full`): every attention and every MoE output is its own source, so the final gate reads 13 sources instead of 7, and the weight logging now separates attention sources from MoE sources. A heatmap follows when it lands. It costs slightly more than block mode; I'll check its ex/s and rerun at a fair step count if it's more than 1% slower.
- **Per-expert hyperball** (`hyperball_per_expert`): the MuonH projection normalizes each routed expert's matrix to its own Frobenius norm. Before, one sphere covered each layer's whole `[E, in, out]` stack, which let norm shift between experts (±3% per step in a toy check). That is one possible route for experts to shrink.
- **MLA KV-latent reuse** (`mla_share_kv_latent`): layer 5 reuses layer 3's normed 512-wide latent, with its own W_uk / W_uv so absorption still works. This halves the MLA KV cache. Shrinking the latent to 256 cost +0.016, so this tests reuse instead.
- **β MLP tuning:** rank 64, and rank 16 on MuonH at 4× (vs 2×).
- **MLA placement** (@ClassicLarry's follow-up): MLA moves to layers 3 and 6, i.e. KDA, KDA, MLA, KDA, KDA, MLA, via a new `global_layers` override. It runs on 2 seeds.
- **Full AttnRes also tests @ClassicLarry's hypothesis** that L5's MLA wants the L3 and L4 attention outputs but not their MoE outputs. The full-mode heatmap gives attention and MoE sources separate columns.
- **d768, learnable qk_mult initialized at 2.5.** Fixed 2.5 gave only −0.0014 at d768 vs −0.009 at d512. This shows where the scalar wants to go at d768.

**Full AttnRes source weights** ([lc1-b15-arfull](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc1-b15-arfull); every attention and MoE output is its own column):

![full AttnRes source weights](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/marin-community/marin/023feb0dd73ce75e202b69cf32b11513bb4855bc/v1/attnres_full_lc1-b15-arfull.png)

Final-step readout:
- **L5's MLA gate (the hypothesis):** L3 MoE 0.21, L2 attn 0.17, L1 MoE 0.11. It avoids L4 MoE (0.03), L3 attn (0.03) and L4 attn (0.08). It does skip back over the most recent sublayers, but not by preferring attention outputs over MoE outputs; its top source is an MoE output (L3's).
- **The general pattern alternates by sublayer type.** Attention gates read the *previous MoE output*: L1 attn → L0 MoE 0.78, L2 attn → L1 MoE 0.57, L4 attn → L3 MoE 0.41. They nearly ignore the previous *attention* output (0.02–0.13). MoE gates read their own layer's attention output (L1 0.49, L4 0.20) plus the previous MoE output.
- **The final gate spreads over the last few sublayers:** L5 MoE 0.26, L4 MoE 0.20, L5 attn 0.14, L4 attn 0.13.

**Takeaway.**
- **Full AttnRes is neutral on loss (−0.0013) and 3% slower** (724 vs about 745 ex/s). At a fair ~2714 steps it would be slightly negative, so block AttnRes stays. The source-type pattern above is the useful output of this run.
- **MLA at layers 3 & 6 is neutral** (+0.0005 / +0.0006 on seeds 0 and 1), so the current placement at 4 & 6 stays.
- **Per-expert hyperball: neutral (+0.0017),** and about 1% slower.
- **KDA β MLP: all 5 variants neutral** (−0.0004 to +0.0023): rank 16 and 64, MuonH 2× and 4×, Adam with random or zero init. The linear β stays.
- **MLA KV-latent reuse costs +0.0056.** L5 reads L3's latent, which halves the MLA KV cache. Halving the latent instead (512 → 256) cost +0.016, so reuse is the cheaper way to shrink the cache if long-context inference memory matters at hero scale. It is not a loss win, so it stays out of the recipe. The **d768 learnable-qk** run is still going.

Every run uses the current best config (qk_mult 2.5 + β1 0.8 + lm_head z-loss 0) with 1% warmup and min LR 0.05× peak; the schedules differ only in shape.

comments.author: ClassicLarry
comments.body:
L4 KDA pays almost zero attention to all prior attention layers. That is suspicious. Perhaps the state tracking nature of KDA gets overwhelmed with too much cross token smearing. Block attention residuals doesn't let KDA layers pick out just the prior MLPs.

Lets try full attention residuals, but block L4 KDA from attending to any prior attention layer outputs. If that improves over the full attention residuals baseline, it indicates an opportunity. We should also assess the impact of dropping sconv from the attention outputs and mlp outputs.

Standard attention residuals follows a 'push' methodology. Each layer output gets to decide what future layers it gets propogated to, since the queries are static per layer. Alternatively, one could use a 'pull' methodology. Every output submodule has a static key, and the query is defined by the current residual stream activation. Lets try that approach, zeroing the keys at init. Also try a hybrid, where we follow standard attn residuals, but just vary the embed. It seems odd that the embed should pre-decide how much it appears in each subsequent layer. To get the embed logit, run a linear projection over the current residual stream. (So we can think of that as the query is the residual stream, and the key is a learned weight).

comments.author: ClassicLarry
comments.body:
🤖 **Batch 18: AttnRes routing structure (@ClassicLarry's latest comment), ShortConv ablations, and a linear-attention variant** (d512, 2817 steps, paired seed 0 on the current bundle with z-loss kept: qk 2.5 + β1 0.8 + no GatedNorms = **3.0854**)

**Addresses** the comment about L4 KDA ignoring earlier attention outputs, the ShortConv ablations, and "pull" vs "push" AttnRes. Branch [`ladderclimb_v1_batch14` @ `5eb01900ba`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/5eb01900ba).

1. **Full AttnRes with L4's KDA attention gate blocked from every earlier attention output** (`attn_res_mask_attn_for=4`). That gate reads only the embedding and the MoE outputs; the masked sources get a −1e9 logit. It is compared against full AttnRes on the same base (`lc1-b18-full`). The batch-15 full run used z-loss 0, so it's rerun here. If the masked version wins, it points to KDA wanting to pick out MoE outputs, which Block AttnRes can't do.
2. **ShortConv ablations:** drop the conv on the attention sublayer output (`sconv_sites=mlp`; only the MLA layers had one, since KDA's output never did), on the MoE output (`sconv_sites=attn`), and both (`sconv_sites=`). KDA's own q/k/v convs stay.
3. **Pull AttnRes** (`attn_res_pull`). Each source has a static learned key k_n, zero-initialized (the running partial has its own). A gate's query is its **current residual stream**: the RMS-normed plain sum of the sources it can see. So logit_n = rms_norm(Σ sources) · k_n. Keys train with Adam at 0.1×, like the push queries. At init it's identical to push (uniform mix).
4. **Hybrid:** push AttnRes, except the **embedding's logit is pulled**: a learned zero-initialized vector per gate, dotted with the gate's RMS-normed current stream (`attn_res_pull_embed`). The embedding no longer pre-decides its weight in each layer.
5. **Gated-DeltaNet-style per-head decay in KDA** (`kda_decay_per_head`): one log-decay per head instead of per channel. This is idea `#5`, a different linear attention.

A depth-1 **MTP** head (idea `#13`: predict t+2 from h_t + W·norm(embed(t+1)) through the shared lm_head, weight 0.3) is implemented at [`06bbf60466`](/06bbf60466). It adds a second lm_head pass, which is expensive at d512, The probe measured 689.6 vs 754.1 ex/s (−8.6%), so it runs at 2576 fixed-time steps.

**Interim.**
- **Full AttnRes on this base: 3.0705, −0.0149.** On the batch-15 base (z-loss 0, GatedNorms kept) it was −0.0013. **At fair fixed-time steps (2712), the two seeds give −0.0080 and +0.0106, a mean of +0.001: no win.** The first result was seed and nondeterminism luck, so block AttnRes stays.
- **Blocking L4's KDA attention gate from earlier attention outputs hurts: +0.0138 vs full AttnRes.** So KDA does want the earlier attention outputs, even though, in full AttnRes, L4's gate ends up weighting mostly the most recent MoE output.
- **Pull AttnRes (+0.0093) and the pulled embedding logit (+0.0071) are both worse**, and both are about 4% slower: each gate has to sum its visible sources for the query. Push AttnRes stays.
- **The ShortConv on attention outputs is removable** (+0.0005, neutral; only the MLA layers had it). Removing the MoE-output ShortConv is slightly worse (+0.0030) despite 1% more speed. Removing both gives +0.0026, which matches the MoE-conv cost. The MoE-output ShortConv earns its keep; the attention-output one does not.
- **GDN-style per-head decay is clearly worse: +0.0129.** KDA's per-channel forget gate matters at no extra speed cost.
- **The first MTP run's eval is invalid.** My MTP term was added inside `next_token_loss`, which the Paloma eval also calls, so the reported eval loss (4.69) included it. Fixed at [`2f06885909`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/2f06885909): training-only terms (MTP, AttnRes z-loss) are now added only in the training step. **The rerun is clearly worse: 3.2272 (+0.14)**, and its mid-run eval is already far behind (3.487 vs ~3.37). With only a linear MTP head and no block of its own, the final hidden state has to serve both t+1 and t+2 through the shared lm_head. DeepSeek's MTP has a full transformer block in that path, which would cost even more at d512. It is also 8.6% slower. MTP was a long shot, tried once and dropped at this rung.

🤖 **Batch 19: a real go at Online KL-Shampoo, applied selectively (@ClassicLarry), and the ShortConv comparison at d768**

**Addresses** the comment asking to give [Online KL-Shampoo](https://blog.tilderesearch.com/blog/online-kl-shampoo) a real go, applied selectively so we can see its direction per matrix family, and to compare dropping all branch-output ShortConvs at d768.

**What the earlier attempt found** (branch `okls-optimizer`, on the pre-KMA baseline). It replaced MuonH on *every* matrix with OKLS's own muP-scaled, AdamC-decayed update. It never beat MuonH (+0.005 to +0.027 over an LR sweep, 16% slower), and its one hyperball variant crashed before step 25. The crash matches the broken-scipy job environment seen elsewhere, so it was never actually tested.

**This version** ([`7d5f5dd116`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/7d5f5dd116)):
- `okls_targets` picks matrix families; everything else stays on MuonH. The families are:
  - **attn**: MLA `w_q/w_o/w_dkv/w_uk/w_uv` and KDA `w_q/w_k/w_v/w_o/w_g`
  - **routed**: the expert gate/up/down stacks
  - **shared**: the shared experts
  - **latent**: the LatentMoE down/up projections
  - **gated_norm**: the GatedNorms
- For the selected matrices, the **direction** is the OKLS whitening `U = S_a^{-1/2} · N · S_b^{-1/2}`. Here N is Nesterov momentum, S_a/S_b are the Kronecker-factor EMAs with the blog's β1 0.9684 / β2 0.9482, and the roots come from 10-step Scaled-CANS coupled Newton-Schulz. **That direction then takes MuonH's hyperball step at the MuonH LR.** Only the direction changes, so there's no new LR scale to tune, and the matrices stay on their Frobenius spheres like the rest of the model.
- CPU checks: the 6 ported OKLS math tests pass (CANS inverse-sqrt accuracy, warm start, whitening conditioning, norm-preserving hyperball step). Routing is verified per family.
- 80-step throughput probes are running for 4 selections. OKLS roots cost O(d³) per matrix, so each gets its own fixed-time step count. Then the full runs go, paired against the current bundle's seed 0 (3.0854):
  - attention only (fp32 CANS)
  - routed experts only (fp16 CANS, since there are 384 small matrices per layer)
  - shared + latent (fp32)
  - all families (fp16)
  - Promising families get LR and β2 variations after that.

**d768 without branch-output ShortConvs** ([lc1-b19-d768-nosc](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lc1-b19-d768-nosc), `sconv_sites=`, 7325 steps) vs the z-loss-kept bundle at d768 (2.8046). At d512 it was +0.0026, and dropping only the attention-output conv was neutral.
